# §0 — Setup

```{r libs}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(MSstatsTMT)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(limma)
  library(vegan)
  library(clusterProfiler)
  library(goseq)
  library(org.Hs.eg.db)         # placeholder; for microbial ORA we'll use
                                # custom TERM2GENE/TERM2NAME tables
  library(AnnotationDbi)
  library(httr2)                # Unipept REST API
  library(jsonlite)
  library(patchwork)
  library(ggrepel)
})

# clusterProfiler and AnnotationDbi both export an S4 select() that masks
# dplyr::select(). filter() is also masked from stats. Pin to dplyr.
select <- dplyr::select
filter <- dplyr::filter
rename <- dplyr::rename
mutate <- dplyr::mutate

set.seed(42)
```

```{r paths}
# ---- Cohort inputs (FragPipe) -------------------------------------------------
# DATA_ROOT is the one path to set; analysis_v17.Rmd reads the same variable.
DATA_ROOT <- Sys.getenv("ICB_DATA_ROOT", "/Volumes/Extreme Pro")
PITT_MSSTATS_CSV   <- file.path(DATA_ROOT, "Metaproteomics/ICB_melanoma_metaproteomics/Pittsbourgh/Results_18_12_25_2/msstats.csv")
PITT_ANNOT_CSV     <- file.path(DATA_ROOT, "Metaproteomics/ICB_melanoma_metaproteomics/Pittsbourgh/Results_18_12_25_2/MSstatsTMT_annotation.csv")
# ^ Confirmed: 8 mixtures (TMT1..TMT8), Conditions = responder / non_responder / Norm / Empty,
#   no Time column (all assumed Pre), 75 non-Empty patients.

SHEBA_PSM_DIR      <- file.path(DATA_ROOT, "Metaproteomics/ICB_melanoma_metaproteomics/Sheba/metagenome_matched/PSMs_combined/")
SHEBA_ANNOT_FILE   <- file.path(SHEBA_PSM_DIR, "MSstatsTMT_annotation_ICB_melanoma.csv")
# ^ Confirmed: 5 mixtures, Mix 1 has TechRepMixture=2, Conditions = Responder /
#   Non_responder / Norm, Time = Pre / Post / Norm. p96 is cross-plex anchor (Mix 1, Mix 3).
#   41 Pre patients (30 R / 11 NR), 8 Post patients (paired Pre/Post via A/B suffix).

# ---- Analysis toggles --------------------------------------------------------
KEEP_POST           <- FALSE   # primary = Pre-only (matches metagenomics).
                               # Set TRUE for the paired Pre/Post secondary analysis.
DROP_EMPTY_CHANNELS <- TRUE    # Pitt has 5 Empty channels — remove pre-summarization.

# ---- Outputs -----------------------------------------------------------------
OUT_DIR <- "Results_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt/metaproteomics"
dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(OUT_DIR, "figures"), showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables"),  showWarnings = FALSE)

# ---- Metagenomics priors -----------------------------------------------------
MG_STATE_PATH <- "Results_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt/metagenomics/metagenomics_combined_state.rds"
mg_state <- if (file.exists(MG_STATE_PATH)) readRDS(MG_STATE_PATH) else {
  warning("Metagenomics state not found at ", MG_STATE_PATH,
          " — §14 cross-omic steps will be skipped.")
  NULL
}
# Expected mg_state fields (verified from str(mg_state, max.level=1)):
#   path_combo, combo_genus (microtable R6), md_combo, m3_res, ld_res, ax_res,
#   m3_path_res, ld_path_res, ax_path_res, verif_genus,
#   alpha_combo_summary, beta_aitch, beta_bray
# The pathway verification tables (verif_pwy, verif_novel) were part of the
# descoped hypothesis layer and are no longer written by the metagenomics
# document; nothing here reads them.
```

```{r resolve_pitt_paths}
stopifnot(file.exists(PITT_MSSTATS_CSV))
stopifnot(file.exists(PITT_ANNOT_CSV))
stopifnot(dir.exists(SHEBA_PSM_DIR))
stopifnot(file.exists(SHEBA_ANNOT_FILE))
```

# §1 — Load FragPipe outputs

The two cohorts enter MSstatsTMT at different stages:

* **Pittsburgh** — `msstats.csv` from TMT-Integrator (post run-normalization). Direct.
* **Sheba** — per-Mixture `psm_*.tsv` from Philosopher (pre-Integrator). Needs
  per-file column reshaping then `PhilosophertoMSstatsTMTFormat()`.

We summarize each cohort *separately* (not a combined input to `proteinSummarization`)
because TMT-Integrator pre-normalizes Pitt but not Sheba — combining them as a
single `msstats.csv` would let Sheba's larger per-plex variance dominate the
median normalization across cohorts.

## §1.0 — Load both annotations

```{r load_annotations}
pitt_annot  <- read.csv(PITT_ANNOT_CSV,  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                        fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
sheba_annot <- read.csv(SHEBA_ANNOT_FILE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                        fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
# (FragPipe-written annotations carry a BOM; the encoding hint avoids a mangled
#  first column name. Recent R handles BOM transparently — drop the arg if it
#  errors.)

required_annot_cols <- c("Run","Fraction","TechRepMixture","Channel",
                         "Condition","Mixture","BioReplicate")
for (label in c("Pitt","Sheba")) {
  ann <- get(if (label == "Pitt") "pitt_annot" else "sheba_annot")
  missing <- setdiff(required_annot_cols, colnames(ann))
  if (length(missing) > 0)
    stop(label, " annotation missing required columns: ",
         paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
}
cat("Pitt  annotation rows:", nrow(pitt_annot),  " | runs:", length(unique(pitt_annot$Run)),  "\n")
cat("Sheba annotation rows:", nrow(sheba_annot), " | runs:", length(unique(sheba_annot$Run)), "\n")
```

## §1.1 — Harmonize, Pre-only filter, inventory

`PhilosophertoMSstatsTMTFormat()` accepts the annotation directly; we want to
pass the already-filtered version (Pre+Norm only, Empty channels removed) so
the converter doesn't process Post rows we'll discard anyway. So this block
runs *before* the data loads.

```{r annot_harmonize}
# Conditions present (verified in uploaded files):
#   Sheba: Responder / Non_responder / Norm
#   Pitt : responder / non_responder / Norm / Empty   (no Time column)
to_binary_response <- function(x) {
  x_norm <- toupper(trimws(x))
  case_when(
    x_norm %in% c("RESPONDER", "R")                    ~ "R",
    x_norm %in% c("NON_RESPONDER","NON-RESPONDER","NR") ~ "NR",
    x_norm == "NORM"                                    ~ "Norm",
    x_norm == "EMPTY"                                   ~ "Empty",
    TRUE                                                ~ NA_character_
  )
}
pitt_annot$Condition_bin  <- to_binary_response(pitt_annot$Condition)
sheba_annot$Condition_bin <- to_binary_response(sheba_annot$Condition)

# Pitt has no Time column — synthesize as "Pre" for non-Norm/Empty rows.
if (!"Time" %in% colnames(pitt_annot)) {
  pitt_annot$Time <- ifelse(pitt_annot$Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR"), "Pre",
                            pitt_annot$Condition_bin)
}
stopifnot(!any(is.na(pitt_annot$Condition_bin)))
stopifnot(!any(is.na(sheba_annot$Condition_bin)))

# Pre-only filter (primary analysis). Norm channels stay (needed by MSstatsTMT
# for cross-mixture normalization). Empty channels in Pitt are dropped.
pre_only_filter <- function(annot, keep_post = FALSE, drop_empty = TRUE) {
  out <- annot
  if (!keep_post) out <- out[out$Time %in% c("Pre","Norm"), , drop = FALSE]
  if (drop_empty) out <- out[out$Condition_bin != "Empty", , drop = FALSE]
  out
}
pitt_annot_use  <- pre_only_filter(pitt_annot,  KEEP_POST, DROP_EMPTY_CHANNELS)
sheba_annot_use <- pre_only_filter(sheba_annot, KEEP_POST, DROP_EMPTY_CHANNELS)
```

```{r inventory}
cat("==== Sheba inventory ====\n")
cat("Mixtures            :", paste(sort(unique(sheba_annot_use$Mixture)), collapse=", "), "\n")
cat("Mix 1 TechRepMixture:", paste(sort(unique(
  sheba_annot_use$TechRepMixture[sheba_annot_use$Mixture == 1])), collapse=", "), "\n")
cat("Pre  R / NR (samples):",
    length(unique(sheba_annot_use$BioReplicate[
      sheba_annot_use$Condition_bin == "R"  & sheba_annot_use$Time == "Pre"])), "/",
    length(unique(sheba_annot_use$BioReplicate[
      sheba_annot_use$Condition_bin == "NR" & sheba_annot_use$Time == "Pre"])), "\n")

cat("\n==== Pittsburgh inventory ====\n")
cat("Mixtures            :", paste(sort(unique(pitt_annot_use$Mixture)), collapse=", "), "\n")
cat("Pre  R / NR (samples):",
    length(unique(pitt_annot_use$BioReplicate[pitt_annot_use$Condition_bin == "R"])), "/",
    length(unique(pitt_annot_use$BioReplicate[pitt_annot_use$Condition_bin == "NR"])), "\n")

# Cross-plex anchors (same BioRep on multiple Mixtures) — only Sheba has these
cross_plex_anchors <- function(annot, label) {
  m <- annot %>% 
    dplyr::filter(Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR")) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(BioReplicate, Mixture) %>% 
    dplyr::count(BioReplicate, name = "n_mixtures") %>%
    dplyr::filter(n_mixtures > 1)
  cat(label, "cross-plex anchors:", 
      if (nrow(m)) paste(m$BioReplicate, collapse=", ") else "NONE", "\n")
}
cross_plex_anchors(sheba_annot_use, "Sheba")
cross_plex_anchors(pitt_annot_use,  "Pitt ")

# §1.3 metadata_join (below) computes the actual metaproteomics-only patient
# list per cohort from mg_state$md_combo — see "Metaproteomics-only patients"
# in the §1.3 diagnostic output.
# Provisional flags: §1.3 overwrites these properly. Set defaults so any
# chunks running before §1.3 don't error on missing columns.
pitt_annot_use$mg_overlap  <- FALSE
sheba_annot_use$mg_overlap <- FALSE
```

> Patient-level metadata (Treatment_regimen, Response double-check) is in
> `mg_state$md_combo` — joined here by BioReplicate after format-bridging.
>
> ID format note (verified):
>  - Pitt metaproteomics : `MF0030`, `MF0071`, ...
>  - Pitt metagenomics   : `MF0030pGTSH10d20221212` (suffix is sequencing batch tag)
>  - Sheba metaproteomics: integer `BioReplicate`, with `A`/`B` suffix on paired
>    Pre/Post patients (`87`, `122A`, ...)
>  - Sheba metagenomics  : `p` + integer + optional `A`/`B`/`_avg` suffix
>    (`p104`, `p87A`, `p96_avg`)
>
> The `_avg` Sheba metagenomics samples are time-averaged Pre+Post for paired
> patients. Our metaproteomics is Pre-only (`KEEP_POST = FALSE`), so we map
> metaproteomics `87` → metagenomics `p87` (or `p87_avg`, stripping the suffix).
> Methodological mismatch worth noting in §14: Pre-only metaproteomics vs
> Pre+Post-averaged metagenomics for the 8 paired-Pre/Post Sheba patients.

```{r metadata_join}
if (!is.null(mg_state)) {
  # ---- Pitt: regex-extract MF prefix ----
  mg_pitt <- mg_state$md_combo %>%
    dplyr::filter(Cohort == "Pitt") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(BioReplicate = stringr::str_extract(SampleID, "^MF\\d+"))

  # ---- Sheba: strip 'p' prefix, keep optional A/B suffix, drop _avg ----
  # "p104"     → "104"
  # "p87A"     → "87A"
  # "p96_avg"  → "96"   (the _avg metagenomics matches the Pre-only metaproteomics)
  mg_sheba <- mg_state$md_combo %>%
    dplyr::filter(Cohort == "Sheba") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(BioReplicate = stringr::str_replace(SampleID,
                                                      "^p(\\d+[AB]?).*", "\\1"))

  # ---- Build join tables ----
  pitt_meta_join <- mg_pitt %>%
    dplyr::transmute(BioReplicate, Treatment_regimen, Response_mg = Response)
  sheba_meta_join <- mg_sheba %>%
    dplyr::transmute(BioReplicate, Treatment_regimen, Response_mg = Response)

  # ---- Apply joins (drop any prior join columns first for idempotency) ----
  pitt_annot_use <- pitt_annot_use %>%
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c("Treatment_regimen","Response_mg","mg_overlap"))) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(pitt_meta_join,  by = "BioReplicate")
  pitt_annot_use$mg_overlap <- !is.na(pitt_annot_use$Treatment_regimen)

  sheba_annot_use <- sheba_annot_use %>%
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c("Treatment_regimen","Response_mg","mg_overlap"))) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(sheba_meta_join, by = "BioReplicate")
  sheba_annot_use$mg_overlap <- !is.na(sheba_annot_use$Treatment_regimen)

  # ---- Diagnostic ----
  cat("==== Cross-omic overlap ====\n")
  cat("Pitt  metaproteomics  :",
      length(unique(pitt_annot_use$BioReplicate[
        pitt_annot_use$Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR")])), "\n")
  cat("Pitt  metagenomics    :", length(unique(mg_pitt$BioReplicate)), "\n")
  cat("Pitt  overlap         :",
      length(unique(pitt_annot_use$BioReplicate[
        pitt_annot_use$mg_overlap & pitt_annot_use$Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR")])), "\n")
  cat("Sheba metaproteomics  :",
      length(unique(sheba_annot_use$BioReplicate[
        sheba_annot_use$Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR")])), "\n")
  cat("Sheba metagenomics    :", length(unique(mg_sheba$BioReplicate)), "\n")
  cat("Sheba overlap         :",
      length(unique(sheba_annot_use$BioReplicate[
        sheba_annot_use$mg_overlap & sheba_annot_use$Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR")])), "\n")

  # Sanity check: Response label agreement between metagenomics and our
  # metaproteomics binary classification (must agree if both used the same RECIST).
  cat("\nResponse-label agreement (overlap subset):\n")
  bind_rows(
    pitt_annot_use  %>% dplyr::filter(mg_overlap, Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR")) %>%
      dplyr::distinct(BioReplicate, Condition_bin, Response_mg) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(Cohort = "Pittsburgh"),
    sheba_annot_use %>% dplyr::filter(mg_overlap, Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR")) %>%
      dplyr::distinct(BioReplicate, Condition_bin, Response_mg) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(Cohort = "Sheba")
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(agree = (Condition_bin == "R" & Response_mg == "Responder") |
                          (Condition_bin == "NR" & Response_mg == "Non_responder")) %>%
    dplyr::count(Cohort, agree) %>% print()

  # Patients in metaproteomics but NOT in metagenomics (will be excluded from §14)
  pitt_mp_only <- setdiff(
    unique(pitt_annot_use$BioReplicate[pitt_annot_use$Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR")]),
    unique(mg_pitt$BioReplicate))
  sheba_mp_only <- setdiff(
    unique(sheba_annot_use$BioReplicate[sheba_annot_use$Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR") &
                                        sheba_annot_use$Time == "Pre"]),
    unique(mg_sheba$BioReplicate))
  cat("\nMetaproteomics-only patients (excluded from §14):\n")
  cat("  Pitt :", length(pitt_mp_only),  "->", paste(pitt_mp_only,  collapse=", "), "\n")
  cat("  Sheba:", length(sheba_mp_only), "->", paste(sheba_mp_only, collapse=", "), "\n")
}
```

## §1.2 — Pittsburgh (Philosopher wide PSM → PhilosophertoMSstatsTMTFormat)

The file FragPipe calls `msstats.csv` for this cohort is actually a Philosopher
*wide-format* PSM table (channels as columns), not a TMT-Integrator long
MSstats file. Same converter as Sheba, just minor column renames.

The Pittsburgh search retained both targets and decoys (the Sheba PSM
preprocessing already filtered decoys upstream, so only Pitt needs the filter).
FragPipe contaminant accessions also slipped through.

```{r load_pitt}
pitt_raw_wide <- read.csv(PITT_MSSTATS_CSV, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cat("Pitt rows (raw):", nrow(pitt_raw_wide),
    " | cols:", ncol(pitt_raw_wide), "\n")

# 1) Channel cols: read.csv mangled the spaces to dots → restore
chan_dot_idx <- grep("^Channel\\.", colnames(pitt_raw_wide))
stopifnot(length(chan_dot_idx) == 11)
colnames(pitt_raw_wide)[chan_dot_idx] <-
  c("Channel 126","Channel 127N","Channel 127C",
    "Channel 128N","Channel 128C","Channel 129N",
    "Channel 129C","Channel 130N","Channel 130C",
    "Channel 131N","Channel 131C")

# 2) Rename to MSstatsTMT-expected column names
names(pitt_raw_wide)[names(pitt_raw_wide) == "Modified.Peptide.Sequence"] <- "Modified.Peptide"
names(pitt_raw_wide)[names(pitt_raw_wide) == "Probability"] <- "PeptideProphetProbability"

# 3) Strip .mzML / .raw from Spectrum.File so it matches annotation Run
pitt_raw_wide$Spectrum.File <- sub("\\.(mzML|raw)$", "",
                                   pitt_raw_wide$Spectrum.File)

# 4) Filter decoys (Pitt only — Sheba was pre-filtered upstream).
#    decoyPyrat used DECOY_ for the microbial side; FragPipe's built-in
#    decoy generator used XXX_ for the human SwissProt subset.
decoy_pattern <- "^DECOY_|^XXX_"
n_decoy <- sum(grepl(decoy_pattern, pitt_raw_wide$Protein))
cat("Pitt decoy PSMs removed:", n_decoy,
    " (", round(100 * n_decoy / nrow(pitt_raw_wide), 2), "%)\n")
pitt_raw_wide <- pitt_raw_wide %>%
  dplyr::filter(!grepl(decoy_pattern, Protein))

# 5) Contaminants — FragPipe Cont_ prefix (chars 4-8 of `sp|Cont_xxxxx|...`)
n_cont <- sum(substr(pitt_raw_wide$Protein, 4, 8) == "Cont_")
if (n_cont > 0) {
  cat("Pitt Cont_ contaminants removed:", n_cont, "\n")
  pitt_raw_wide <- pitt_raw_wide %>%
    dplyr::filter(substr(Protein, 4, 8) != "Cont_")
}

# 6) Run-overlap sanity check
overlap <- intersect(unique(pitt_raw_wide$Spectrum.File),
                     unique(pitt_annot_use$Run))
cat("Pitt Run overlap PSM <-> annotation:", length(overlap), "/",
    length(unique(pitt_annot_use$Run)), "\n")
stopifnot(length(overlap) >= length(unique(pitt_annot_use$Run)) - 1)

# 7) Convert to MSstatsTMT long format
pitt_raw <- PhilosophertoMSstatsTMTFormat(
  input                      = pitt_raw_wide,
  annotation                 = pitt_annot_use,
  protein_id_col             = "Protein",
  Purity_cutoff              = 0.6,
  PeptideProphet_prob_cutoff = 0.7,
  rmPeptide_OxidationM       = TRUE,
  useUniquePeptide           = TRUE,
  rmPSM_withfewMea_withinRun = TRUE,
  rmProtein_with1Feature     = FALSE,
  summaryforMultipleRows     = sum,
  use_log_file               = FALSE,
  verbose                    = TRUE
)
pitt_raw <- pitt_raw[!is.na(pitt_raw$Condition), ]
cat("Pitt MSstats-format rows:", nrow(pitt_raw),
    " | unique proteins:", length(unique(pitt_raw$ProteinName)), "\n")
```

## §1.3 — Sheba (per-Mixture psm.tsv → PhilosophertoMSstatsTMTFormat)

The Sheba search ran without TMT-Integrator, so each Mixture has a separate
`psm_*.tsv` with intensity columns named `Intensity sample-XX` / `pool-XX`
rather than `channel 126…131C`. We rename **per file** to TMT channels (positional
— FragPipe writes channels in 126→131C order within each Mixture's PSM table)
and only then `bind_rows`. Binding first would let FragPipe's collision suffix
on duplicate sample names (`-01b` etc.) eat half the channels.

```{r load_sheba}
# 1) Load each PSM file into a list, keyed by short name
sheba_psm_files <- list.files(SHEBA_PSM_DIR,
                              pattern = "^psm.*\\.tsv$",
                              full.names = TRUE)
cat("Sheba PSM files:", length(sheba_psm_files), "\n")
print(basename(sheba_psm_files))

df_input_list <- lapply(sheba_psm_files, function(f) {
  vroom::vroom(f, show_col_types = FALSE)
})
names(df_input_list) <- gsub(basename(sheba_psm_files),
                             pattern = "\\..*", replacement = "")

# 2) Drop non-MSstats PSM columns
columns_to_remove <- c(
  "Extended Peptide", "Prev AA", "Next AA", "Peptide Length",
  "Retention", "Observed Mass", "Calibrated Observed Mass",
  "Observed M/Z", "Calibrated Observed M/Z",
  "Calculated Observed Mass", "Calculated Peptide Mass",
  "Calculated M/Z", "Delta Mass", "SpectralSim", "RTScore",
  "Expectation", "Hyperscore", "Nextscore",
  "Number of Enzymatic Termini", "Number of Missed Cleavages",
  "Assigned Modifications", "Observed Modifications",
  "Entry Name", "Qvalue", "Quan Usage", "Is Decoy", "Is Contaminant",
  "Parent Scan Number", "Apex Retention Time", "Apex Scan Number",
  "Retention Time Start", "Retention Time End",
  "Retention Time FWHM", "Traced Scans"
)
df_input_list <- lapply(df_input_list, function(x) {
  x[!(names(x) %in% columns_to_remove)]
})

# 3) Rename first 17 columns to MSstats-friendly names (drops dots/spaces)
colnames_for_df <- c("Spectrum.Name", "Spectrum.File", "Peptide.Sequence",
                     "Modified.Peptide", "Charge", "PeptideProphetProbability",
                     "Protein.Start", "Protein.End", "Intensity", "Purity",
                     "Is.Unique", "Protein", "Protein.ID", "Gene",
                     "Protein.Description", "Mapped.Genes", "Mapped.Proteins")
df_input_list <- lapply(df_input_list, function(df) {
  colnames(df)[1:17] <- colnames_for_df[1:17]; df
})

# 4) Reorder so the 11 channel-intensity columns end up at positions 18:28
df_input_list <- lapply(df_input_list, function(X) {
  X[c('Spectrum.Name','Spectrum.File','Peptide.Sequence','Modified.Peptide',
      'PeptideProphetProbability','Charge','Protein.Start','Protein.End',
      'Gene','Mapped.Genes','Protein','Protein.ID','Mapped.Proteins',
      'Protein.Description','Is.Unique','Purity','Intensity',
      colnames(X)[18:28])]
})

# 5) Strip "interact-" / ".pep.xml" from Spectrum.File so it matches annot$Run
df_input_list <- lapply(df_input_list, function(x) {
  x$Spectrum.File <- stringr::str_remove(x$Spectrum.File, "\\.pep\\.xml$")
  x$Spectrum.File <- stringr::str_remove(x$Spectrum.File, "^interact-")
  x
})

# 6) Per-file rename intensity columns at positions 18:28 to TMT channel labels.
#    POSITIONAL — assumes FragPipe writes channels in 126→131C order in each
#    Mixture's PSM table. If you ever re-search with a non-standard channel
#    order, this will need a per-file lookup.
tmt_channels <- c("Channel 126","Channel 127N","Channel 127C",
                  "Channel 128N","Channel 128C","Channel 129N",
                  "Channel 129C","Channel 130N","Channel 130C",
                  "Channel 131N","Channel 131C")
df_input_list <- lapply(df_input_list, function(x) {
  names(x)[18:28] <- tmt_channels; x
})

# 7) Combine all PSM files
sheba_psm_combined <- bind_rows(df_input_list)

# 8) Drop FragPipe contaminants. Accessions look like sp|Cont_xxxxx|... so
#    chars 4-8 of the Protein string are "Cont_".
#    Decoy filter — Sheba's PSMs were pre-filtered upstream (decoyPyrat with
#    DECOY_ prefix), so we expect zero matches; the check is defensive.
n_decoy_sheba <- sum(grepl("^DECOY_|^DECOY-|^rev_|^REV_|###REV###",
                           sheba_psm_combined$Protein))
if (n_decoy_sheba > 0) {
  cat("Sheba decoy PSMs found and removed:", n_decoy_sheba, "\n")
  sheba_psm_combined <- sheba_psm_combined %>%
    dplyr::filter(!grepl("^DECOY_|^DECOY-|^rev_|^REV_|###REV###", Protein))
} else {
  cat("Sheba: no decoys present (already filtered upstream).\n")
}
sheba_psm_combined <- sheba_psm_combined %>%
  dplyr::filter(substr(Protein, 4, 8) != "Cont_")
cat("Sheba PSMs after decoy + contaminant filter:", nrow(sheba_psm_combined),
    " | unique runs in PSMs:",
    length(unique(sheba_psm_combined$Spectrum.File)), "\n")

# Sanity check — Spectrum.File values should match annot$Run
overlap <- intersect(unique(sheba_psm_combined$Spectrum.File),
                     unique(sheba_annot_use$Run))
cat("Run overlap PSM <-> annotation:", length(overlap), "/",
    length(unique(sheba_annot_use$Run)), "\n")
stopifnot(length(overlap) > 0)

# 9) Convert to MSstatsTMT format. Note: parameter is `protein_id_col` (current
#    MSstatsTMT API), not `which.proteinid` (older API).
sheba_raw <- PhilosophertoMSstatsTMTFormat(
  input                      = sheba_psm_combined,
  annotation                 = sheba_annot_use,
  protein_id_col             = "Protein",
  Purity_cutoff              = 0.6,
  PeptideProphet_prob_cutoff = 0.7,
  rmPeptide_OxidationM       = TRUE,
  useUniquePeptide           = TRUE,
  rmPSM_withfewMea_withinRun = TRUE,
  rmProtein_with1Feature     = FALSE,   # consistent per-cohort filter in §4
  summaryforMultipleRows     = sum,
  use_log_file               = FALSE,
  verbose                    = TRUE
)
sheba_raw <- sheba_raw[!is.na(sheba_raw$Condition), ]
cat("Sheba MSstats-format rows:", nrow(sheba_raw),
    " | unique proteins:", length(unique(sheba_raw$ProteinName)), "\n")

# Mixture is integer for Sheba (1..5) but character for Pitt (TMT1..TMT8).
# Standardize to character cohort-wide so downstream Sample-key joins don't
# need per-site coercion.
sheba_annot_use$Mixture <- as.character(sheba_annot_use$Mixture)
pitt_annot_use$Mixture  <- as.character(pitt_annot_use$Mixture)
```

## §1.4 — Functional annotation, microbial/host split, KO mapping

The two cohorts use **independent Prokka assemblies** (Sheba: `KMMIBAFL_*` +
`PPAAKGPG_*`; Pitt: `OIDECCNN_*`). There is therefore zero protein-ID overlap
between cohorts by construction, even where orthologs exist. This means:

1. Per-cohort DA stays at the Prokka-protein level (§7-§8).
2. **Cross-cohort DA must operate on a shared functional vocabulary** — KEGG
   Orthology (KO) terms from eggNOG-mapper (§9, §11-§13).
3. Cross-cohort taxonomic comparison uses Unipept LCA on tryptic peptides,
   which is sequence-based and DB-agnostic (§10).

```{r eggnog_paths}
DATA_ROOT <- Sys.getenv("ICB_DATA_ROOT", "/Volumes/Extreme Pro")
PITT_EGGNOG  <- file.path(DATA_ROOT, "Proteomic_databases/ICB_melanoma_Pittsbourgh/prokka_gut_meta/eggnog_prokka_Pittsbourgh.tsv.emapper.annotations")
SHEBA_EGGNOG <- file.path(DATA_ROOT, "Proteomic_databases/ICB_melanoma_Sheba/ICB_melanoma_genome_matched/eggnog_annotations_combined.tsv")
stopifnot(file.exists(PITT_EGGNOG))
stopifnot(file.exists(SHEBA_EGGNOG))
```

### §1.4.1 — Load eggNOG-mapper outputs

```{r eggnog_load}
read_eggnog <- function(path) {
  # Header line starts with `#query`; preceded by `## ` comment lines that
  # vary between emapper versions. Find the header by scanning.
  lines <- readLines(path, n = 100)
  header_idx <- which(startsWith(lines, "#query"))[1]
  if (is.na(header_idx))
    stop("Couldn't find #query header in ", path)

  df <- read.delim(path,
                   skip            = header_idx - 1,
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                   na.strings      = c("-", "NA", ""),
                   quote           = "",
                   comment.char    = "")
  names(df)[1] <- "query"   # was "#query" or "X.query"
  df
}

pitt_eggnog  <- read_eggnog(PITT_EGGNOG)
sheba_eggnog <- read_eggnog(SHEBA_EGGNOG)

cat("Pitt eggNOG annotations :", nrow(pitt_eggnog),
    " | columns:", ncol(pitt_eggnog), "\n")
cat("Sheba eggNOG annotations:", nrow(sheba_eggnog),
    " | columns:", ncol(sheba_eggnog), "\n")
stopifnot(identical(sort(colnames(pitt_eggnog)), sort(colnames(sheba_eggnog))))
```

### §1.4.2 — Verify Sheba covers both Prokka prefixes

```{r eggnog_sheba_prefix_check}
sheba_eggnog_prefix <- stringr::str_extract(sheba_eggnog$query, "^[A-Z]+_")
cat("Sheba eggNOG query-prefix distribution:\n")
print(table(sheba_eggnog_prefix, useNA = "ifany"))
# Expect both KMMIBAFL_ and PPAAKGPG_ in roughly the proportions seen in
# unique(sheba_raw$ProteinName) (KMMIBAFL ~43%, PPAAKGPG ~57%). If only one
# prefix is present, the eggNOG file is incomplete and we'd need to
# concatenate the two assembly-specific files.
```

### §1.4.3 — Microbial / host protein classification

```{r protein_class}
prefix_class <- function(p) {
  case_when(
    grepl("^sp\\|",                p) ~ "Human_SwissProt",
    grepl("^tr\\|",                p) ~ "Human_TrEMBL",
    grepl("^PPAAKGPG_|^KMMIBAFL_", p) ~ "Sheba_Prokka",
    grepl("^OIDECCNN_",            p) ~ "Pitt_Prokka",
    TRUE                              ~ "Other"
  )
}

# Verified counts (paste from your run):
#   Sheba: 6836 Sheba_Prokka, 355 Human_SwissProt, 3 Human_TrEMBL
#   Pitt:  10576 Pitt_Prokka, 577 Human_SwissProt, 6 Human_TrEMBL, 6 Other
# Inspect the 6 Pitt "Other" proteins — usually contaminants without Cont_ prefix
pitt_other_ids <- pitt_raw %>%
  filter(prefix_class(ProteinName) == "Other") %>%
  distinct(ProteinName) %>% pull(ProteinName)
if (length(pitt_other_ids) > 0) {
  cat("Pitt 'Other' proteins (excluded from analysis):\n")
  print(pitt_other_ids)
}

# Microbial subset for §3-§13 main pipeline. Host subset saved for optional §16.
pitt_raw_microbial  <- pitt_raw  %>% filter(prefix_class(ProteinName) == "Pitt_Prokka")
sheba_raw_microbial <- sheba_raw %>% filter(prefix_class(ProteinName) == "Sheba_Prokka")
pitt_raw_host  <- pitt_raw  %>% filter(prefix_class(ProteinName) %in% c("Human_SwissProt","Human_TrEMBL"))
sheba_raw_host <- sheba_raw %>% filter(prefix_class(ProteinName) %in% c("Human_SwissProt","Human_TrEMBL"))

cat("\nPost-split row counts:\n")
cat("  Pitt  microbial:", nrow(pitt_raw_microbial),  " | host:", nrow(pitt_raw_host),  "\n")
cat("  Sheba microbial:", nrow(sheba_raw_microbial), " | host:", nrow(sheba_raw_host), "\n")
```

### §1.4.4 — eggNOG annotation coverage

```{r eggnog_coverage}
sheba_microbial_ids <- unique(sheba_raw_microbial$ProteinName)
pitt_microbial_ids  <- unique(pitt_raw_microbial$ProteinName)

cat("Sheba microbial proteins  :", length(sheba_microbial_ids), "\n")
cat("  in eggNOG annotation table:", sum(sheba_microbial_ids %in% sheba_eggnog$query),
    " (", round(100 * mean(sheba_microbial_ids %in% sheba_eggnog$query), 1), "%)\n")

cat("Pitt  microbial proteins  :", length(pitt_microbial_ids), "\n")
cat("  in eggNOG annotation table:", sum(pitt_microbial_ids %in% pitt_eggnog$query),
    " (", round(100 * mean(pitt_microbial_ids %in% pitt_eggnog$query), 1), "%)\n")

# Per-prefix coverage (Sheba only, since two assemblies)
sheba_coverage_by_prefix <- tibble(
  ProteinName = sheba_microbial_ids,
  prefix      = stringr::str_extract(sheba_microbial_ids, "^[A-Z]+_"),
  in_eggnog   = sheba_microbial_ids %in% sheba_eggnog$query
) %>% group_by(prefix) %>%
  summarise(n_proteins   = n(),
            n_annotated  = sum(in_eggnog),
            pct_covered  = round(100 * mean(in_eggnog), 1),
            .groups = "drop")
print(sheba_coverage_by_prefix)
# Both prefixes should be covered at roughly the same rate. If one is at ~0%
# while the other is at ~80%, the eggNOG_combined.tsv only covers one assembly
# and we need to concatenate.
```

### §1.4.5 — Build long-format KO mapping per cohort

```{r ko_mapping}
build_ko_mapping <- function(eggnog_df) {
  eggnog_df %>%
    dplyr::select(query, KEGG_ko) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(KEGG_ko)) %>%
    tidyr::separate_rows(KEGG_ko, sep = ",") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(KO = stringr::str_remove(KEGG_ko, "^ko:")) %>%
    dplyr::select(KO, ProteinID = query) %>%
    dplyr::distinct() %>%
    dplyr::filter(KO != "", !is.na(KO))
}

pitt_ko_map  <- build_ko_mapping(pitt_eggnog)
sheba_ko_map <- build_ko_mapping(sheba_eggnog)

cat("Pitt KO mapping:\n")
cat("  rows                   :", nrow(pitt_ko_map), "\n")
cat("  unique KOs             :", length(unique(pitt_ko_map$KO)), "\n")
cat("  proteins with ≥1 KO    :", length(unique(pitt_ko_map$ProteinID)), "\n")

cat("\nSheba KO mapping:\n")
cat("  rows                   :", nrow(sheba_ko_map), "\n")
cat("  unique KOs             :", length(unique(sheba_ko_map$KO)), "\n")
cat("  proteins with ≥1 KO    :", length(unique(sheba_ko_map$ProteinID)), "\n")

# Cross-cohort KO universe — this is the substrate for §11-§13 combined DA
ko_intersect <- intersect(unique(pitt_ko_map$KO), unique(sheba_ko_map$KO))
ko_union     <- union(unique(pitt_ko_map$KO),     unique(sheba_ko_map$KO))
cat("\nKO universe:\n")
cat("  union (any cohort)     :", length(ko_union), "\n")
cat("  intersection (both)    :", length(ko_intersect),
    " (", round(100 * length(ko_intersect) / length(ko_union), 1), "% of union)\n")
```

### §1.4.6 — Restrict KO map to observed proteins

The eggNOG files cover the full upstream Prokka FASTA — ~2.2M ORFs for Sheba,
~520K for Pitt. Only ~7K Sheba and ~10K Pitt proteins were observed in MS.
For enrichment analysis (§9) and cross-cohort KO-level DA (§11-§13), the
"background universe" must be observed proteins — otherwise GSEA/ORA loses
all calibration.

We keep the full KO maps around for §10 Unipept (peptide-level taxonomy uses
the full database as the search space), but create observed-restricted versions
for everything else.

```{r ko_map_observed}
pitt_ko_map_obs  <- pitt_ko_map  %>% dplyr::filter(ProteinID %in% pitt_microbial_ids)
sheba_ko_map_obs <- sheba_ko_map %>% dplyr::filter(ProteinID %in% sheba_microbial_ids)

cat("Pitt observed:\n")
cat("  rows               :", nrow(pitt_ko_map_obs), "\n")
cat("  unique KOs         :", length(unique(pitt_ko_map_obs$KO)), "\n")
cat("  proteins w/ ≥1 KO  :", length(unique(pitt_ko_map_obs$ProteinID)),
    " /", length(pitt_microbial_ids),
    " (", round(100 * length(unique(pitt_ko_map_obs$ProteinID)) /
                       length(pitt_microbial_ids), 1), "%)\n")

cat("\nSheba observed:\n")
cat("  rows               :", nrow(sheba_ko_map_obs), "\n")
cat("  unique KOs         :", length(unique(sheba_ko_map_obs$KO)), "\n")
cat("  proteins w/ ≥1 KO  :", length(unique(sheba_ko_map_obs$ProteinID)),
    " /", length(sheba_microbial_ids),
    " (", round(100 * length(unique(sheba_ko_map_obs$ProteinID)) /
                       length(sheba_microbial_ids), 1), "%)\n")

ko_obs_intersect <- intersect(unique(pitt_ko_map_obs$KO),
                              unique(sheba_ko_map_obs$KO))
ko_obs_union     <- union(unique(pitt_ko_map_obs$KO),
                          unique(sheba_ko_map_obs$KO))
cat("\nObserved KO universe:\n")
cat("  union              :", length(ko_obs_union), "\n")
cat("  intersection       :", length(ko_obs_intersect),
    " (", round(100 * length(ko_obs_intersect) / length(ko_obs_union), 1), "%)\n")

# Per-KO multiplicity sanity check
cat("\nMedian proteins-per-KO:\n")
cat("  Pitt  observed     :", median(table(pitt_ko_map_obs$KO)),  "\n")
cat("  Sheba observed     :", median(table(sheba_ko_map_obs$KO)), "\n")
```

### §1.4.7 — Switch working datasets to microbial-only

```{r restrict_microbial}
# Keep originals around in case §16 host analysis is added later
pitt_raw_full  <- pitt_raw
sheba_raw_full <- sheba_raw
pitt_raw       <- pitt_raw_microbial
sheba_raw      <- sheba_raw_microbial

cat("Working datasets are now microbial-only:\n")
cat("  Pitt  rows:", nrow(pitt_raw),
    " | proteins:", length(unique(pitt_raw$ProteinName)), "\n")
cat("  Sheba rows:", nrow(sheba_raw),
    " | proteins:", length(unique(sheba_raw$ProteinName)), "\n")

# Note: ~6% Pitt and ~6% Sheba microbial proteins lack any KO annotation.
# These stay in pitt_raw / sheba_raw for per-cohort §3-§8 (summarization,
# ordination, per-cohort DA) but drop out of §9 enrichment and §11-§13
# cross-cohort DA, which both subset on KO-mapped proteins.
```

### §1.4.8 — KEGG_Pathway mapping (primary cross-cohort substrate)

KO-level cross-cohort DA is statistically unstable here because the FASTA
was clustered at 90% identity (`prokka_90.faa`) — median 2 proteins per KO.
We therefore use **KEGG pathway map** as the primary cross-cohort vocabulary
(median ~12-23 proteins/pathway) and reserve KO-level tests for specific
hypothesis-driven subsets in the §14 verdicts.

```{r pathway_mapping}
build_pathway_mapping <- function(eggnog_df) {
  eggnog_df %>%
    dplyr::select(query, KEGG_Pathway) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(KEGG_Pathway)) %>%
    tidyr::separate_rows(KEGG_Pathway, sep = ",") %>%
    # eggNOG outputs both "ko02020" (KO-level) and "map02020" (pathway-map)
    # forms; they're synonyms. Standardize on map*.
    dplyr::mutate(KEGG_Pathway = stringr::str_replace(KEGG_Pathway, "^ko", "map")) %>%
    dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(KEGG_Pathway, "^map\\d+")) %>%
    dplyr::select(Pathway = KEGG_Pathway, ProteinID = query) %>%
    dplyr::distinct()
}

pitt_pw_map  <- build_pathway_mapping(pitt_eggnog)
sheba_pw_map <- build_pathway_mapping(sheba_eggnog)

# Restrict to MS-observed proteins
pitt_pw_map_obs  <- pitt_pw_map  %>% dplyr::filter(ProteinID %in% pitt_microbial_ids)
sheba_pw_map_obs <- sheba_pw_map %>% dplyr::filter(ProteinID %in% sheba_microbial_ids)

cat("Pitt observed pathways  :", length(unique(pitt_pw_map_obs$Pathway)),
    "  | median proteins/pathway:", median(table(pitt_pw_map_obs$Pathway)), "\n")
cat("Sheba observed pathways :", length(unique(sheba_pw_map_obs$Pathway)),
    "  | median proteins/pathway:", median(table(sheba_pw_map_obs$Pathway)), "\n")

pw_obs_intersect <- intersect(unique(pitt_pw_map_obs$Pathway),
                              unique(sheba_pw_map_obs$Pathway))
pw_obs_union     <- union(unique(pitt_pw_map_obs$Pathway),
                          unique(sheba_pw_map_obs$Pathway))
cat("\nPathway intersection    :", length(pw_obs_intersect),
    "  (substrate for §11-§13 cross-cohort DA)\n")
cat("Pathway union           :", length(pw_obs_union), "\n")

# Filter to "well-covered" pathways (≥5 proteins observed in BOTH cohorts).
# This is what we'll actually use for combined-cohort DA — pathways with
# only 1-2 observed proteins are noisy.
pathway_protein_counts <- tibble(Pathway = pw_obs_intersect) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_pitt  = sapply(Pathway, function(p) sum(pitt_pw_map_obs$Pathway  == p)),
    n_sheba = sapply(Pathway, function(p) sum(sheba_pw_map_obs$Pathway == p))
  )
well_covered_pathways <- pathway_protein_counts %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_pitt >= 5, n_sheba >= 5) %>%
  dplyr::pull(Pathway)
cat("Pathways with ≥5 observed proteins in both cohorts:",
    length(well_covered_pathways), "\n")
```

# §2 — QC

## §2.1 — PSM-level QC

```{r psm_qc, fig.height=4}
qc_intensity_dist <- function(df, cohort) {
  df %>%
    filter(!is.na(Intensity), Intensity > 0) %>%
    mutate(logI = log2(Intensity)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = Run, y = logI, fill = Run)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3) +
    labs(title = paste(cohort, "— log2 PSM intensity by run"),
         x = NULL, y = "log2 intensity") +
    theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none",
                       axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 6))
}
p_pitt_qc  <- qc_intensity_dist(pitt_raw,  "Pittsburgh")
p_sheba_qc <- qc_intensity_dist(sheba_raw, "Sheba")
p_pitt_qc / p_sheba_qc
# Pitt: 8 mixtures × 5 fractions = 40 runs (one extra in TMT2 — see annot row 60).
# Sheba: ~30 runs total. Mix 1 has TechRepMixture=2 → 10 of the runs are tech-rep
# pairs (FS1_LL_18613_* vs FS1_18006_LL_*), expected to be tightly correlated.
```

## §2.2 — Per-channel missingness

```{r channel_missing, fig.height=4}
channel_missing <- function(df, cohort) {
  df %>%
    group_by(Run, Channel) %>%
    summarise(pct_missing = mean(is.na(Intensity) | Intensity <= 0) * 100,
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = Channel, y = Run, fill = pct_missing)) +
    geom_tile() + scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C") +
    labs(title = paste(cohort, "— % missing per channel×run"),
         fill = "% missing") +
    theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}
channel_missing(pitt_raw,  "Pittsburgh")
channel_missing(sheba_raw, "Sheba")
```

## §2.3 — Cross-plex anchor (p96) and Mix-1 TechRepMixture QC (Sheba only)

p96 is measured in Mix 1 *and* Mix 3 (both Pre, both NR). MSstatsTMT will use
this as a biological anchor for cross-mixture normalization automatically — no
manual averaging needed. The QC question is whether p96's protein abundances
agree across the two mixtures after summarization (§3 below). Mix 1's
TechRepMixture=2 gives a separate within-mixture technical-replicate variance
estimate Pitt lacks.

```{r p96_diag}
# Cross-plex anchor inventory
p96_rows <- sheba_annot_use %>%
  filter(BioReplicate == "96")
print(p96_rows %>% distinct(Mixture, TechRepMixture, Channel, Condition_bin, Time))
# Expected: Mix 1 / Mix 3, both Pre/NR.

# Mix 1 TechRepMixture=2 inventory — within-mixture tech replicate
mix1_rows <- sheba_annot_use %>%
  filter(Mixture == 1) %>%
  distinct(TechRepMixture, Run) %>% arrange(TechRepMixture, Run)
print(mix1_rows)
# Tech-rep correlation will be computed in §3.3 once the summarized matrix exists.
```

# §3 — Protein summarization (MSstatsTMT)

`global_norm + reference_norm` together perform **all** the cross-mixture
batch correction we need. `MBimpute = FALSE` so missingness propagates to
downstream methods that handle it natively (limma per-feature, ordination
via complete-case subset). No ComBat anywhere — that would be double-correction
on top of `reference_norm` (issue #2 from the metagenomics handoff).

```{r summarize, cache=TRUE}

pitt_sum <- proteinSummarization(
  data                 = pitt_raw,
  method               = "msstats",
  global_norm          = TRUE,
  reference_norm       = TRUE,
  remove_norm_channel  = TRUE,
  remove_empty_channel = TRUE,
  MBimpute             = FALSE,
  use_log_file         = FALSE
)

sheba_sum <- proteinSummarization(
  data                 = sheba_raw,
  method               = "msstats",
  global_norm          = TRUE,
  reference_norm       = TRUE,
  remove_norm_channel  = TRUE,
  remove_empty_channel = TRUE,
  MBimpute             = FALSE,
  use_log_file         = FALSE
)

shape_report <- function(sum_obj, label) {
  pld <- sum_obj$ProteinLevelData
  pld$Sample <- paste(pld$Mixture, pld$Channel, sep = "_")
  cat(label, ": ", length(unique(pld$Protein)), " proteins × ",
      length(unique(pld$Sample)), " samples,  ",
      round(100 * mean(is.na(pld$Abundance)), 1), "% missing\n", sep = "")
}
shape_report(pitt_sum,  "Pitt ")
shape_report(sheba_sum, "Sheba")
```

## §3.1 — Mixture-effect QC (did `reference_norm` work?)

```{r mixture_effect_qc, fig.height=4}
# Per-mixture median post-summarization. Should be ~0 (within ±0.2). Outlier
# mixtures suggest residual mixture structure that needs explicit modeling
# in §7 (limma `+ factor(Mixture)`).
mixture_effect_check <- function(sum_obj, label) {
  cat("====", label, "per-mixture median post-summarization ====\n")
  sum_obj$ProteinLevelData %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Mixture) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(median_abundance = round(median(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
                     n_proteins       = length(unique(Protein)),
                     n_channels       = length(unique(Channel)),
                     .groups = "drop") %>%
    print()
}
mixture_effect_check(pitt_sum,  "Pitt")
mixture_effect_check(sheba_sum, "Sheba")

# Visual: per-Mixture boxplot of summarized abundances. Heads-up flags from
# pre-summarization diagnostics:
#   Sheba Mix 5 had Pool log2I = 12.6 (lowest); samples were also low — should
#     normalize cleanly via reference_norm.
#   Pitt TMT7 had Pool log2I = 15.1 (highest); ~40% missingness on TMT7-127N.
#     If TMT7 still sits offset post-summarization, model Mixture in §7.
mixture_qc_plot <- function(sum_obj, label) {
  sum_obj$ProteinLevelData %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Abundance)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = Mixture, y = Abundance, fill = Mixture)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3) +
    labs(title = paste(label, "— summarized abundance by Mixture (post reference_norm)"),
         y = "log2 abundance", x = NULL) +
    theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none")
}
mixture_qc_plot(pitt_sum,  "Pittsburgh") /
  mixture_qc_plot(sheba_sum, "Sheba")
```

## §3.2 — Long → wide matrix

```{r sum_to_matrix}
long_to_matrix <- function(prot_long) {
  # Sheba Mix 1 has TechRepMixture = 1 + 2 → same (Protein, Sample) key appears
  # twice; pivot_wider would pack the two values into a list cell. Average
  # them at the long-format stage to preserve numeric matrix class.
  wide <- prot_long %>%
    dplyr::transmute(Protein,
                     Sample    = paste(Mixture, Channel, sep = "_"),
                     Abundance = as.numeric(Abundance)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Protein, Sample) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(Abundance = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
                     .groups   = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Abundance = ifelse(is.nan(Abundance), NA_real_, Abundance)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from  = Sample,
                       values_from = Abundance,
                       values_fill = NA_real_)
  m <- as.matrix(wide[, -1])
  storage.mode(m) <- "double"   # forces numeric coercion; NA stays NA
  rownames(m) <- wide$Protein
  m
}
pitt_mat  <- long_to_matrix(pitt_sum$ProteinLevelData)
sheba_mat <- long_to_matrix(sheba_sum$ProteinLevelData)

# Verify numeric storage and report missingness on the WIDE matrix
# (long-format missingness is misleading — see §3.1 note).
cat("Pitt  matrix: ", dim(pitt_mat),  " | typeof=", typeof(pitt_mat),
    " | missing=", round(100*mean(is.na(pitt_mat)),1), "%\n", sep="")
cat("Sheba matrix: ", dim(sheba_mat), " | typeof=", typeof(sheba_mat),
    " | missing=", round(100*mean(is.na(sheba_mat)),1), "%\n", sep="")

# Quantile of detected values — sanity check on the abundance scale
cat("\nPitt  detected-value quantiles:\n")
print(round(quantile(pitt_mat,  c(0.01, 0.05, 0.5, 0.95, 0.99), na.rm=TRUE), 2))
cat("Sheba detected-value quantiles:\n")
print(round(quantile(sheba_mat, c(0.01, 0.05, 0.5, 0.95, 0.99), na.rm=TRUE), 2))
```

# §4 — Filtering

```{r filter}
# Per-cohort: keep proteins detected in ≥50% of samples in that cohort.
#
# The sample axis is the per-cohort wide matrix from §3.2 (proteins × samples).
# Detection rate operates on the WIDE matrix because §3 long-format hides
# cross-mixture missingness (proteins not detected in a mixture get no row,
# so the long-format missingness rate is misleading).
filter_by_detection <- function(mat, min_detection = 0.5) {
  detected <- rowMeans(!is.na(mat)) >= min_detection
  mat[detected, , drop = FALSE]
}
pitt_mat_f  <- filter_by_detection(pitt_mat,  0.5)
sheba_mat_f <- filter_by_detection(sheba_mat, 0.5)

cat("Pitt  proteins kept :", nrow(pitt_mat_f),  "/", nrow(pitt_mat),
    " (", round(100 * nrow(pitt_mat_f)/nrow(pitt_mat),  1), "%)\n")
cat("Sheba proteins kept :", nrow(sheba_mat_f), "/", nrow(sheba_mat),
    " (", round(100 * nrow(sheba_mat_f)/nrow(sheba_mat), 1), "%)\n")

# Detection-rate distribution per cohort (sanity)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(rowMeans(!is.na(pitt_mat)),  breaks = 40, xlab = "detection rate",
     main = "Pitt — pre-filter")
abline(v = 0.5, col = "red", lty = 2)
hist(rowMeans(!is.na(sheba_mat)), breaks = 40, xlab = "detection rate",
     main = "Sheba — pre-filter")
abline(v = 0.5, col = "red", lty = 2)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Cross-cohort intersection by Prokka ID is meaningless (different assemblies)
# — see §1.4. Combined-cohort analysis happens at the KEGG_Pathway level in
# §11-§13 using the protein × KO/Pathway maps from §1.4.5/§1.4.8.
```

# §5 — Ordination (β-diversity analog)

The metagenomics priors (handoff §6): Cohort effect on β-diversity is large,
Response effect is essentially null (R² = 0.6%, p = 0.97 stratified-Aitchison
combined). Expectation here: same shape — Cohort dominates over Response,
and within each cohort, biological structure (if any) is on PC2 or beyond.

```{r pca_per_cohort, fig.height=4.5}
pca_complete_proteins <- function(mat, annot) {
  complete <- mat[complete.cases(mat), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(complete) < 50)
    warning("Few complete-case proteins (", nrow(complete),
            ") — consider 80% detection threshold.")
  pr <- prcomp(t(complete), scale. = TRUE)
  scores <- as.data.frame(pr$x[, 1:2])
  scores$Sample <- rownames(scores)
  scores <- scores %>%
    tidyr::separate(Sample, into = c("Mixture","Channel"),
                    sep = "_", remove = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(annot %>% dplyr::distinct(Mixture, Channel,
                                               Condition_bin, BioReplicate),
                     by = c("Mixture","Channel"))
  list(pca = pr, scores = scores,
       n_complete = nrow(complete),
       var_explained = summary(pr)$importance[2, 1:2])
}
pitt_pca  <- pca_complete_proteins(pitt_mat_f,  pitt_annot_use)
sheba_pca <- pca_complete_proteins(sheba_mat_f, sheba_annot_use)

cat("Pitt  complete-case proteins :", pitt_pca$n_complete, "\n")
cat("Sheba complete-case proteins :", sheba_pca$n_complete, "\n")

plot_pca <- function(res, cohort) {
  ve <- res$var_explained * 100
  ggplot(res$scores, aes(PC1, PC2, color = Condition_bin, shape = Mixture)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
    labs(title = paste0(cohort, " — PCA (complete-case proteins, n=",
                        res$n_complete, ")"),
         x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%%)", ve[1]),
         y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%%)", ve[2])) +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02"))
}
plot_pca(pitt_pca,  "Pittsburgh") | plot_pca(sheba_pca, "Sheba")
```

```{r permanova}
# PERMANOVA — log-abundance Euclidean (the proteomic analog of Aitchison).
# §3.1 confirmed per-mixture medians within ±0.3 log2 — no need for
# `+ factor(Mixture)` in the per-cohort PERMANOVA.
run_permanova <- function(mat, annot, formula_rhs, perm = 999) {
  complete <- mat[complete.cases(mat), , drop = FALSE]
  meta <- annot %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Sample = paste(Mixture, Channel, sep = "_")) %>%
    dplyr::filter(Sample %in% colnames(complete),
                  Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR"))
  meta <- meta[match(colnames(complete)[colnames(complete) %in% meta$Sample],
                     meta$Sample), ]
  mat_use <- complete[, meta$Sample, drop = FALSE]
  d <- dist(t(mat_use), method = "euclidean")
  f <- as.formula(paste("d ~", formula_rhs))
  adonis2(f, data = meta, by = "margin", permutations = perm)
}
permanova_pitt  <- run_permanova(pitt_mat_f,  pitt_annot_use,  "Condition_bin")
permanova_sheba <- run_permanova(sheba_mat_f, sheba_annot_use, "Condition_bin")
cat("==== Pitt PERMANOVA ====\n");  print(permanova_pitt)
cat("\n==== Sheba PERMANOVA ====\n"); print(permanova_sheba)

# Combined-cohort PERMANOVA: at the protein level the cohorts have ~zero
# overlap (different Prokka assemblies). The combined ordination would only
# make sense at the KEGG_Pathway level — deferred to §11-§13.
# Once Treatment_regimen is joined: replace formula_rhs with
# "Condition_bin + Treatment_regimen" to match metagenomics covariate set.
```

# §7–§8 — Per-cohort differential abundance

Three-method consensus, paralleling metagenomics §10–§12:

1. **MSstatsTMT** `groupComparison()` (primary; mixed-effects on summarized features)
2. **limma** on the summarized log-abundance matrix (independent statistical model)
3. **Permutation test** on log-abundance with same covariate set

Per-cohort criterion, the same rule the metagenomics document applies to its
own three methods: a protein passes only if it has nominal support (p<0.10) in
≥1 method per cohort with concordant direction.

## §7.1 — MSstatsTMT::groupComparisonTMT (per cohort)

```{r msstats_da, cache=TRUE}
# =============================================================================
# §7.1 — MSstatsTMT groupComparisonTMT (per cohort, microbial-only)
# =============================================================================
# Method 1 of 3 in the consensus. Internally fits a mixed-effects model with
# Mixture and TechRepMixture as random effects, so the §7.2/§7.3 mixture
# correction is matched.
#
# Operates on the SUMMARIZED long-format object (pitt_sum / sheba_sum), not
# the matrix. Restrict to microbial proteins (already done at §1.4.7) and
# to R/NR samples only (Norm channels were removed by remove_norm_channel
# = TRUE in §3, so this is largely already the case).

run_msstats_da <- function(sum_obj, annot, label) {
  pld <- sum_obj$ProteinLevelData
  pld$Sample <- paste(pld$Mixture, pld$Channel, sep = "_")

  # Restrict to R/NR samples (drop any residual)
  rn_samples <- annot %>%
    dplyr::filter(Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR")) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(Mixture, Channel, Condition_bin) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Mixture = as.character(Mixture),
                  Channel = as.character(Channel),
                  Sample  = paste(Mixture, Channel, sep = "_"))

  pld_rn <- pld %>% dplyr::filter(Sample %in% rn_samples$Sample)

  # Recode Condition to R/NR for the contrast
  pld_rn <- pld_rn %>%
    dplyr::left_join(rn_samples %>% dplyr::select(Sample, Condition_bin),
                     by = "Sample") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Condition = Condition_bin) %>%
    dplyr::select(-Sample, -Condition_bin)

  # Mirror the structure groupComparisonTMT expects on the input slot
  sum_for_da <- sum_obj
  sum_for_da$ProteinLevelData <- pld_rn
  # FeatureLevelData restricted similarly
  fld <- sum_obj$FeatureLevelData
  fld$Sample <- paste(fld$Mixture, fld$Channel, sep = "_")
  fld_rn <- fld %>% dplyr::filter(Sample %in% rn_samples$Sample)
  fld_rn <- fld_rn %>%
    dplyr::left_join(rn_samples %>% dplyr::select(Sample, Condition_bin),
                     by = "Sample") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Condition = Condition_bin) %>%
    dplyr::select(-Sample, -Condition_bin)
  sum_for_da$FeatureLevelData <- fld_rn

  # Contrast: R - NR
  contrast <- matrix(c(-1, 1), nrow = 1, dimnames = list("R_vs_NR", c("NR","R")))

  cat(label, "— running groupComparisonTMT (mixed-effects, may take 3-8 min)...\n",
      sep="")
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  msstats_res <- MSstatsTMT::groupComparisonTMT(
    data           = sum_for_da,
    contrast.matrix = contrast,
    moderated       = TRUE,
    adj.method      = "BH",
    remove_norm_channel = TRUE,
    remove_empty_channel = TRUE,
    save_fitted_models  = FALSE,
    use_log_file        = FALSE
  )
  cat(label, "— elapsed: ",
      round(as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units="mins"), 1), " min\n", sep="")

  # Tidy
  cmp <- msstats_res$ComparisonResult %>%
    dplyr::filter(Label == "R_vs_NR") %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      Protein   = as.character(Protein),
      logFC_ms  = log2FC,        # already log2 scale (Abundance was log2)
      SE_ms     = SE,
      df_ms     = DF,
      p_ms      = pvalue,
      q_ms      = adj.pvalue,
      issue     = issue
    )
  cat(label, "— MSstatsTMT summary: ",
      sum(cmp$q_ms < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " at q<0.10, ",
      sum(cmp$p_ms < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " at p<0.10, ",
      sum(!is.na(cmp$issue)), " flagged with issues\n", sep="")
  if (sum(!is.na(cmp$issue)) > 0) {
    cat(label, "— issue types: ",
        paste(names(table(cmp$issue)), collapse=", "), "\n", sep="")
  }
  cmp
}

pitt_msstats  <- run_msstats_da(pitt_sum,  pitt_annot_use,  "Pitt ")
sheba_msstats <- run_msstats_da(sheba_sum, sheba_annot_use, "Sheba")
```

## §7.2 — limma on summarized matrix (per cohort)

```{r limma_da}
# =============================================================================
# §7.2 — limma per cohort, mixture-controlled
# =============================================================================
# Primary model: ~ 0 + Condition_bin + factor(Mixture)
# Treatment_regimen NOT included at per-cohort level (no confound; reserved
# for combined §11-§13). Mixture-as-fixed-effect rationale: §5 PERMANOVA
# revealed Mixture R² = 0.35-0.38 in both cohorts despite §3.1 per-mixture
# median flatness — reference_norm corrects per-mixture location but not
# protein-by-protein covariance structure across batches.

limma_da <- function(mat, annot, label, min_per_group = 3) {
  # 1. Build sample metadata from matrix columns
  sm <- tibble::tibble(Sample = colnames(mat)) %>%
    tidyr::separate(Sample, into = c("Mixture","Channel"),
                    sep = "_", remove = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      annot %>% dplyr::distinct(Mixture, Channel, Condition_bin, BioReplicate),
      by = c("Mixture","Channel"))

  # 2. Restrict to R/NR samples (drops any residual Norm if present)
  keep <- sm$Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR") & !is.na(sm$Condition_bin)
  sm   <- sm[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  y    <- mat[, sm$Sample, drop = FALSE]

  # 3. Per-mixture R/NR balance — flag mixtures with one class only
  bal <- table(sm$Mixture, sm$Condition_bin)
  cat(label, "— per-mixture R/NR balance:\n", sep="")
  print(bal)
  degenerate_mix <- rownames(bal)[apply(bal, 1, function(r) any(r < min_per_group))]
  if (length(degenerate_mix) > 0) {
    cat(label, "— mixtures with <", min_per_group,
        " in one class:", paste(degenerate_mix, collapse=", "), "\n", sep="")
    cat(label, "— these contribute no within-mixture R-vs-NR contrast power.\n",
        sep="")
  }

  # 4. Build design + contrast
  cond <- factor(sm$Condition_bin, levels = c("NR","R"))   # contrast = R - NR
  mix  <- factor(sm$Mixture)
  design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + cond + mix)
  colnames(design) <- sub("^cond", "", colnames(design))
  contr <- limma::makeContrasts(R_vs_NR = R - NR, levels = design)

  # 5. Fit
  fit  <- limma::lmFit(y, design)
  fit2 <- limma::contrasts.fit(fit, contr)
  fit2 <- limma::eBayes(fit2, trend = TRUE, robust = TRUE)

  # 6. Tidy output
  tt <- limma::topTable(fit2, coef = "R_vs_NR", number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
  res <- tibble::tibble(
    Protein   = rownames(y),
    logFC     = tt$logFC,
    AveExpr   = tt$AveExpr,
    t         = tt$t,
    p_limma   = tt$P.Value,
    q_limma   = tt$adj.P.Val,
    n_obs     = rowSums(!is.na(y))
  )

  cat(label, "— limma summary: ",
      sum(res$q_limma < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " at q<0.10, ",
      sum(res$p_limma < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " at p<0.10, n=",
      ncol(y), " samples × ", nrow(y), " proteins\n", sep="")

  list(res = res, design = design, sm = sm, y = y)
}

pitt_limma  <- limma_da(pitt_mat_f,  pitt_annot_use,  "Pitt ")
sheba_limma <- limma_da(sheba_mat_f, sheba_annot_use, "Sheba")


# §7.2b — limma WITHOUT factor(Mixture), as a sensitivity / outer bound
limma_da_nomix <- function(mat, annot, label) {
  sm <- tibble::tibble(Sample = colnames(mat)) %>%
    tidyr::separate(Sample, into = c("Mixture","Channel"),
                    sep = "_", remove = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      annot %>% dplyr::distinct(Mixture, Channel, Condition_bin, BioReplicate),
      by = c("Mixture","Channel"))
  keep <- sm$Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR") & !is.na(sm$Condition_bin)
  sm <- sm[keep, , drop = FALSE]; y <- mat[, sm$Sample, drop = FALSE]
  cond <- factor(sm$Condition_bin, levels = c("NR","R"))
  design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + cond)
  colnames(design) <- sub("^cond", "", colnames(design))
  contr <- limma::makeContrasts(R_vs_NR = R - NR, levels = design)
  fit  <- limma::lmFit(y, design)
  fit2 <- limma::eBayes(limma::contrasts.fit(fit, contr), trend = TRUE, robust = TRUE)
  tt   <- limma::topTable(fit2, coef = "R_vs_NR", number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
  res  <- tibble::tibble(Protein = rownames(y),
                         logFC_nomix = tt$logFC, p_nomix = tt$P.Value,
                         q_nomix = tt$adj.P.Val)
  cat(label, "— limma (no Mixture): ",
      sum(res$q_nomix < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " at q<0.10, ",
      sum(res$p_nomix < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " at p<0.10\n", sep="")
  res
}
pitt_limma_nomix  <- limma_da_nomix(pitt_mat_f,  pitt_annot_use,  "Pitt ")
sheba_limma_nomix <- limma_da_nomix(sheba_mat_f, sheba_annot_use, "Sheba")
```

## §7.3 — Permutation test (per cohort)

```{r perm_da, cache=TRUE}
# =============================================================================
# §7.3 — Permutation test, within-Mixture stratified (corrected)
# =============================================================================
# Strategy: per-protein, fit Mixture-only OLS on observed (non-NA) samples,
# take residuals on those samples, compute R-vs-NR mean diff. Permute
# Condition_bin within Mixture and repeat.
#
# This is slower (per-protein lm) but correct under arbitrary missingness
# patterns, including proteins entirely absent from a Mixture.

permutation_da <- function(limma_obj, label, n_perm = 999, seed = 42,
                           min_obs_per_class = 3) {
  set.seed(seed)
  y    <- limma_obj$y
  sm   <- limma_obj$sm
  cond <- factor(sm$Condition_bin, levels = c("NR","R"))
  mix  <- factor(sm$Mixture)
  n_p  <- nrow(y); n_s <- ncol(y)

  cat(label, "— ", n_perm, " perms × ", n_p, " proteins × ", n_s, " samples\n",
      sep="")

  obs_stat <- rep(NA_real_, n_p)
  null_stat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_p, ncol = n_perm)

  # The within-mixture shuffle is done by ave(cond_obs, mxi, FUN = sample)
  # inside the loop below, on the OBSERVED subset of each protein, so there is
  # nothing to pre-build here: the index sets differ protein by protein.

  t0 <- Sys.time()
  for (i in seq_len(n_p)) {
    yi <- y[i, ]
    keep <- which(!is.na(yi))

    # Skip if either class has <min_obs_per_class observed samples after NA removal
    cls <- cond[keep]
    if (sum(cls == "R") < min_obs_per_class ||
        sum(cls == "NR") < min_obs_per_class) next

    # Need at least 2 mixtures with observations and ≥1 sample per class somewhere
    mxi <- droplevels(mix[keep])
    if (nlevels(mxi) < 2) next

    # Mixture-residualized response
    yi_obs   <- yi[keep]
    cond_obs <- droplevels(cls)
    mix_resid <- residuals(lm(yi_obs ~ mxi))   # contains only observed positions

    # Observed: R-mean minus NR-mean of residuals
    obs_stat[i] <- mean(mix_resid[cond_obs == "R"]) -
                   mean(mix_resid[cond_obs == "NR"])

    # Permute cond WITHIN mixture, on the observed subset
    for (k in seq_len(n_perm)) {
      cond_perm <- ave(as.character(cond_obs), mxi, FUN = sample)
      null_stat[i, k] <- mean(mix_resid[cond_perm == "R"]) -
                         mean(mix_resid[cond_perm == "NR"])
    }
    if (i %% 200 == 0) cat("  protein ", i, "/", n_p, "\n", sep="")
  }
  cat(label, "— elapsed: ",
      round(as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units="secs"), 1), "s\n", sep="")

  # Two-sided permutation p
  abs_obs <- abs(obs_stat)
  n_ge    <- rowSums(abs(null_stat) >= abs_obs, na.rm = TRUE)
  n_valid <- rowSums(!is.na(null_stat))
  p_perm  <- ifelse(n_valid > 0, (n_ge + 1) / (n_valid + 1), NA_real_)
  q_perm  <- p.adjust(p_perm, method = "BH")

  res <- tibble::tibble(
    Protein  = rownames(y),
    diff_RvsNR = obs_stat,
    p_perm   = p_perm,
    q_perm   = q_perm,
    n_perms_valid = n_valid
  )
  cat(label, "— permutation summary: ",
      sum(res$q_perm < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " at q<0.10, ",
      sum(res$p_perm < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " at p<0.10, ",
      sum(is.na(res$p_perm)), " skipped (insufficient observations)\n", sep="")
  res
}

pitt_perm  <- permutation_da(pitt_limma,  "Pitt ", n_perm = 999)
sheba_perm <- permutation_da(sheba_limma, "Sheba", n_perm = 999)


permutation_da_nomix <- function(limma_obj, label, n_perm = 999, seed = 42,
                                  min_obs_per_class = 3) {
  set.seed(seed)
  y <- limma_obj$y; sm <- limma_obj$sm
  cond <- factor(sm$Condition_bin, levels = c("NR","R"))
  n_p <- nrow(y); n_s <- ncol(y)
  cat(label, "— ", n_perm, " perms × ", n_p, " proteins × ", n_s, " samples (no Mixture)\n", sep="")

  obs_stat  <- rep(NA_real_, n_p)
  null_stat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_p, ncol = n_perm)

  t0 <- Sys.time()
  for (i in seq_len(n_p)) {
    yi <- y[i, ]; keep <- which(!is.na(yi))
    cls <- cond[keep]
    if (sum(cls == "R") < min_obs_per_class ||
        sum(cls == "NR") < min_obs_per_class) next
    yi_obs <- yi[keep]; cond_obs <- droplevels(cls)
    obs_stat[i] <- mean(yi_obs[cond_obs == "R"]) -
                   mean(yi_obs[cond_obs == "NR"])
    for (k in seq_len(n_perm)) {
      cond_perm <- sample(cond_obs)
      null_stat[i, k] <- mean(yi_obs[cond_perm == "R"]) -
                         mean(yi_obs[cond_perm == "NR"])
    }
    if (i %% 200 == 0) cat("  protein ", i, "/", n_p, "\n", sep="")
  }
  cat(label, "— elapsed: ",
      round(as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units="secs"), 1), "s\n", sep="")

  abs_obs <- abs(obs_stat)
  n_ge    <- rowSums(abs(null_stat) >= abs_obs, na.rm = TRUE)
  n_valid <- rowSums(!is.na(null_stat))
  p_nomix <- ifelse(n_valid > 0, (n_ge + 1) / (n_valid + 1), NA_real_)
  q_nomix <- p.adjust(p_nomix, method = "BH")

  res <- tibble::tibble(Protein = rownames(y),
                        diff_RvsNR_nomix = obs_stat,
                        p_perm_nomix = p_nomix,
                        q_perm_nomix = q_nomix)
  cat(label, "— permutation (no Mixture): ",
      sum(res$q_perm_nomix < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " at q<0.10, ",
      sum(res$p_perm_nomix < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " at p<0.10\n", sep="")
  res
}

pitt_perm_nomix  <- permutation_da_nomix(pitt_limma,  "Pitt ")
sheba_perm_nomix <- permutation_da_nomix(sheba_limma, "Sheba")


par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
hist(pitt_perm$p_perm,        breaks = 50, main = "Pitt: p_perm (Mixture-cond)")
hist(pitt_perm_nomix$p_perm_nomix,  breaks = 50, main = "Pitt: p_perm (no Mixture)")
hist(sheba_perm$p_perm,       breaks = 50, main = "Sheba: p_perm (Mixture-cond)")
hist(sheba_perm_nomix$p_perm_nomix, breaks = 50, main = "Sheba: p_perm (no Mixture)")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

cat("Pitt  perms valid (cond) :", paste(range(pitt_perm$n_perms_valid), collapse="-"), "\n")
cat("Sheba perms valid (cond) :", paste(range(sheba_perm$n_perms_valid), collapse="-"), "\n")
```

## §7.4 — Three-method consensus per cohort

A protein is a per-cohort "consensus hit" if it has nominal support
(p<0.10) in ≥2 of 3 methods with directional concordance. This mirrors the
metagenomics document's three-method consensus (MaAsLin3 + LinDA + ALDEx2).

```{r consensus}
# =============================================================================
# §7.4 — Three-method per-cohort consensus
# =============================================================================
# Primary methods: limma (no Mixture) + permutation (no Mixture) + MSstatsTMT.
# Sensitivity:    limma (Mixture-cond) + permutation (Mixture-cond), reported
# alongside primary as a robustness check against the random TMT plex
# imbalance (TMT5 = 0 NR / 10 R, etc.). Plex assignment was random but
# unstratified, so unconditional is the appropriate primary; conditional
# is the sensitivity bound.
#
# Tier 1: q<0.10 in ≥2 of the 3 primary methods, concordant direction.
# Tier 2: p<0.10 in ≥2 of the 3 primary methods, concordant direction.
# Robust subset: Tier 1 hits that also reach p<0.10 in BOTH sensitivity methods.

build_consensus <- function(limma_nomix_res, perm_nomix_res, ms_res,
                             limma_cond_res, perm_cond_res, label) {
  d <- limma_nomix_res %>%
    dplyr::select(Protein, logFC_nomix, p_nomix, q_nomix) %>%
    dplyr::rename(logFC_lim = logFC_nomix, p_lim = p_nomix, q_lim = q_nomix) %>%
    dplyr::full_join(
      perm_nomix_res %>% dplyr::select(Protein,
                                        diff_RvsNR_nomix,
                                        p_perm_nomix, q_perm_nomix),
      by = "Protein") %>%
    dplyr::full_join(
      ms_res %>% dplyr::select(Protein, logFC_ms, p_ms, q_ms),
      by = "Protein") %>%
    dplyr::full_join(
      limma_cond_res$res %>% dplyr::select(Protein, p_limma, q_limma) %>%
        dplyr::rename(p_lim_cond = p_limma, q_lim_cond = q_limma),
      by = "Protein") %>%
    dplyr::full_join(
      perm_cond_res %>% dplyr::select(Protein, p_perm, q_perm) %>%
        dplyr::rename(p_perm_cond = p_perm, q_perm_cond = q_perm),
      by = "Protein")

  # Direction consensus across the three primaries
  dir_lim  <- sign(d$logFC_lim)
  dir_perm <- sign(d$diff_RvsNR_nomix)
  dir_ms   <- sign(d$logFC_ms)
  d$concordant_dir <- (
    !is.na(dir_lim) & !is.na(dir_perm) & dir_lim == dir_perm
  ) & (
    is.na(dir_ms) | dir_ms == dir_lim   # MS direction agrees if available
  )

  d$n_methods_q10 <- (!is.na(d$q_lim) & d$q_lim < 0.10) +
                     (!is.na(d$q_perm_nomix) & d$q_perm_nomix < 0.10) +
                     (!is.na(d$q_ms) & d$q_ms < 0.10)

  d$n_methods_p10 <- (!is.na(d$p_lim) & d$p_lim < 0.10) +
                     (!is.na(d$p_perm_nomix) & d$p_perm_nomix < 0.10) +
                     (!is.na(d$p_ms) & d$p_ms < 0.10)

  d$tier1 <- d$n_methods_q10 >= 2 & d$concordant_dir
  d$tier2 <- d$n_methods_p10 >= 2 & d$concordant_dir & !d$tier1

  # Sensitivity check: Tier 1 hits also hold under Mixture-conditional
  d$robust <- d$tier1 &
              !is.na(d$p_lim_cond)  & d$p_lim_cond  < 0.10 &
              !is.na(d$p_perm_cond) & d$p_perm_cond < 0.10

  cat("==== ", label, " consensus ====\n", sep="")
  cat("  Tier 1 (q<0.10 in ≥2/3 + concordant): ", sum(d$tier1, na.rm=TRUE), "\n")
  cat("    of which robust to Mixture-cond  : ", sum(d$robust, na.rm=TRUE), "\n")
  cat("  Tier 2 (p<0.10 in ≥2/3 + concordant): ", sum(d$tier2, na.rm=TRUE), "\n")
  cat("  Direction breakdown of Tier 1:\n")
  print(table(R_up = d$logFC_lim[d$tier1] > 0, useNA = "ifany"))
  d
}

pitt_consensus  <- build_consensus(
  limma_nomix_res = pitt_limma_nomix,     # 57 q<0.10 (primary)
  perm_nomix_res  = pitt_perm_nomix,      # 19 q<0.10 (primary)
  ms_res          = pitt_msstats,         # 0  q<0.10 (primary, weak)
  limma_cond_res  = pitt_limma,           # the Mixture-cond limma object
  perm_cond_res   = pitt_perm,            # the Mixture-cond permutation
  label           = "Pitt ")
sheba_consensus <- build_consensus(sheba_limma_nomix, sheba_perm_nomix,
                                    sheba_msstats,
                                    sheba_limma, sheba_perm, "Sheba")

# Save Tier 1 for §8 / §14
readr::write_csv(
  pitt_consensus  %>% dplyr::filter(tier1) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(q_lim, p_perm_nomix),
  file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "pitt_tier1_consensus.csv"))
readr::write_csv(
  sheba_consensus %>% dplyr::filter(tier1 | tier2) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(p_lim, p_perm_nomix),
  file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "sheba_tier1_tier2_consensus.csv"))
```

# §8 — Per-cohort DA — diagnostics & save

```{r per_cohort_save}
# =============================================================================
# §8 — Per-cohort volcano + Tier 1 reporting
# =============================================================================
# Volcanos use the PRIMARY (unconditional) limma logFC + p-value, with
# Tier 1 / Tier 2 / robust-to-Mixture-cond shading. Pitt has 17 Tier 1;
# Sheba has 0 Tier 1 / 86 Tier 2 — Sheba volcano shades Tier 2 in absence
# of Tier 1.

library(ggplot2)

build_volcano_df <- function(consensus, label) {
  consensus %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(logFC_lim), !is.na(p_lim)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      neglog10p = -log10(p_lim),
      tier = dplyr::case_when(
        robust ~ "Tier 1 (robust)",
        tier1  ~ "Tier 1",
        tier2  ~ "Tier 2",
        TRUE   ~ "Other"),
      tier = factor(tier, levels = c("Other", "Tier 2", "Tier 1", "Tier 1 (robust)")),
      Cohort = label
    )
}

pitt_vol_df  <- build_volcano_df(pitt_consensus,  "Pittsburgh")
sheba_vol_df <- build_volcano_df(sheba_consensus, "Sheba")

volcano_plot <- function(df, label, label_top_n = 10) {
  pal <- c("Other" = "grey80", "Tier 2" = "#FFB000",
           "Tier 1" = "#DC267F", "Tier 1 (robust)" = "#000000")

  top_lab <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(tier %in% c("Tier 1", "Tier 1 (robust)")) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(p_lim) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = label_top_n) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      pitt_eggnog %>% dplyr::select(query, Preferred_name) %>% dplyr::distinct(),
      by = c("Protein" = "query"))

  ggplot(df, aes(x = logFC_lim, y = neglog10p, colour = tier)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_point(data = df %>% dplyr::filter(tier == "Other"),
               size = 0.6, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_point(data = df %>% dplyr::filter(tier != "Other"),
               size = 1.6, alpha = 0.9) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      data = top_lab,
      aes(label = ifelse(is.na(Preferred_name),
                         stringr::str_remove(Protein, "^OIDECCNN_"),
                         Preferred_name)),
      size = 2.8, max.overlaps = 20, box.padding = 0.4,
      min.segment.length = 0, segment.colour = "grey70",
      colour = "black") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = pal, name = NULL) +
    labs(title    = label,
         subtitle = paste0("Tier 1: ", sum(df$tier == "Tier 1") +
                                       sum(df$tier == "Tier 1 (robust)"),
                          " (", sum(df$tier == "Tier 1 (robust)"),
                          " robust)  |  Tier 2: ", sum(df$tier == "Tier 2")),
         x = expression(log[2]*"FC (R - NR)"),
         y = expression(-log[10]*italic("p"))) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"))
}

p_pitt_vol  <- volcano_plot(pitt_vol_df,  "Pittsburgh — protein-level R vs NR")
p_sheba_vol <- volcano_plot(sheba_vol_df, "Sheba — protein-level R vs NR", label_top_n = 6)

p_combined_vol <- p_pitt_vol + p_sheba_vol + patchwork::plot_layout(ncol = 2)
```
