# =============================================================================
# §9 — KEGG_Pathway enrichment (per cohort)
# =============================================================================
# Two complementary methods on the same KEGG_Pathway substrate:
#   §9.1 ORA  via clusterProfiler::enricher (hypergeometric, on Tier 1+2 union)
#   §9.2 GSEA via clusterProfiler::GSEA      (rank-based, on full sorted logFC)
#   §9.3 goSeq with peptide-count bias correction
#
# Background = ALL proteins tested per cohort (= rownames of *_mat_f), not
# the union of cohort matrices, since Prokka assemblies don't share protein
# IDs across cohorts.
#
# DE selection criteria:
#   ORA / goSeq:  Tier 1 ∪ Tier 2 (concordant_dir==TRUE), per-direction subsets
#   GSEA:         all tested proteins, ranked by signed logFC * -log10(p_lim)
```{r}
# ---- §9.0 — KEGG pathway name lookup --------------------------------------
# Build a Pathway → human-readable name map. eggNOG outputs pathway IDs
# without names; pull names via KEGGREST (cached locally).
kegg_pathway_names <- local({
  cache_path <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "kegg_pathway_names.tsv")
  if (file.exists(cache_path)) {
    readr::read_tsv(cache_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  } else {
    if (!requireNamespace("KEGGREST", quietly = TRUE)) {
      cat("KEGGREST not installed — using pathway IDs as names.\n")
      tibble::tibble(Pathway = character(), Name = character())
    } else {
      pathway_ids <- union(unique(pitt_pw_map_obs$Pathway),
                           unique(sheba_pw_map_obs$Pathway))
      cat("Fetching KEGG pathway names for ", length(pathway_ids), " IDs ...\n",
          sep = "")
      # Batch in groups of 10 (KEGGREST limit)
      batches <- split(pathway_ids, ceiling(seq_along(pathway_ids) / 10))
      name_list <- list()
      for (b in batches) {
        res <- tryCatch(KEGGREST::keggGet(b),
                        error = function(e) { Sys.sleep(2); KEGGREST::keggGet(b) })
        for (entry in res) {
          name_list[[paste0("map", entry$ENTRY)]] <- entry$NAME[1]
        }
        Sys.sleep(0.3)  # politeness
      }
      tbl <- tibble::tibble(Pathway = names(name_list),
                            Name    = unlist(name_list))
      readr::write_tsv(tbl, cache_path)
      tbl
    }
  }
})
cat("KEGG pathway names cached: ", nrow(kegg_pathway_names), "\n", sep = "")

# ---- §9.1 — ORA (per direction) -------------------------------------------
ora_directional <- function(consensus, pw_map_obs, mat_f, pathway_names,
                             label, direction = c("R_up","NR_up","Any")) {
  direction <- match.arg(direction)
  base <- consensus$tier1 | consensus$tier2
  if (direction == "R_up")  sig <- base & consensus$logFC_lim > 0
  if (direction == "NR_up") sig <- base & consensus$logFC_lim < 0
  if (direction == "Any")   sig <- base
  sig_proteins <- consensus$Protein[sig & !is.na(sig)]
  background   <- rownames(mat_f)

  if (length(sig_proteins) < 5) {
    cat(label, " ORA (", direction, "): too few significant (", length(sig_proteins),
        ") — skipped\n", sep = "")
    return(NULL)
  }

  term2gene <- pw_map_obs %>% dplyr::select(Pathway, ProteinID)
  term2name <- pathway_names

  res <- tryCatch(
    clusterProfiler::enricher(
      gene          = sig_proteins,
      universe      = background,
      TERM2GENE     = term2gene,
      TERM2NAME     = term2name,
      pvalueCutoff  = 1, qvalueCutoff = 1,   # don't filter inside; we threshold later
      minGSSize     = 3, maxGSSize    = 500),
    error = function(e) { cat(label, "ORA error:", e$message, "\n"); NULL }
  )

  if (is.null(res) || nrow(as.data.frame(res)) == 0) {
    cat(label, " ORA (", direction, "): no enrichment\n", sep = "")
    return(NULL)
  }

  df <- as.data.frame(res) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(Pathway = ID, Name = Description,
                     n_sig = Count, GeneRatio, BgRatio,
                     p_ora = pvalue, q_ora = p.adjust,
                     direction = direction, cohort = label)
  cat(label, " ORA (", direction, "): ",
      sum(df$q_ora < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " pathways at q<0.10, ",
      sum(df$p_ora < 0.05, na.rm=TRUE), " at p<0.05\n", sep = "")
  df
}

pitt_ora_R   <- ora_directional(pitt_consensus,  pitt_pw_map_obs,  pitt_mat_f,  kegg_pathway_names, "Pitt ", "R_up")
pitt_ora_NR  <- ora_directional(pitt_consensus,  pitt_pw_map_obs,  pitt_mat_f,  kegg_pathway_names, "Pitt ", "NR_up")
sheba_ora_R  <- ora_directional(sheba_consensus, sheba_pw_map_obs, sheba_mat_f, kegg_pathway_names, "Sheba", "R_up")
sheba_ora_NR <- ora_directional(sheba_consensus, sheba_pw_map_obs, sheba_mat_f, kegg_pathway_names, "Sheba", "NR_up")

ora_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(pitt_ora_R, pitt_ora_NR, sheba_ora_R, sheba_ora_NR)

# ---- §9.2 — GSEA (rank-based, on full logFC*-log10p ranking) ---------------
gsea_pathway <- function(consensus, pw_map_obs, pathway_names, label) {
  ranks <- consensus %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(logFC_lim), !is.na(p_lim)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(score = sign(logFC_lim) * -log10(p_lim)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(score))
  rank_vec <- setNames(ranks$score, ranks$Protein)

  res <- tryCatch(
    clusterProfiler::GSEA(
      geneList     = rank_vec,
      TERM2GENE    = pw_map_obs %>% dplyr::select(Pathway, ProteinID),
      TERM2NAME    = pathway_names,
      pvalueCutoff = 1,
      minGSSize    = 5, maxGSSize = 500,
      eps          = 0,
      seed         = TRUE,
      verbose      = FALSE),
    error = function(e) { cat(label, "GSEA error:", e$message, "\n"); NULL }
  )

  if (is.null(res) || nrow(as.data.frame(res)) == 0) {
    cat(label, " GSEA: no enrichment\n"); return(NULL)
  }

  df <- as.data.frame(res) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(Pathway = ID, Name = Description,
                     NES, p_gsea = pvalue, q_gsea = p.adjust,
                     direction = ifelse(NES > 0, "R_up", "NR_up"),
                     cohort = label)
  cat(label, " GSEA: ",
      sum(df$q_gsea < 0.10), " pathways at q<0.10, ",
      sum(df$p_gsea < 0.05), " at p<0.05\n", sep = "")
  df
}

pitt_gsea  <- gsea_pathway(pitt_consensus,  pitt_pw_map_obs,  kegg_pathway_names, "Pitt ")
sheba_gsea <- gsea_pathway(sheba_consensus, sheba_pw_map_obs, kegg_pathway_names, "Sheba")
gsea_all   <- dplyr::bind_rows(pitt_gsea, sheba_gsea)

# ---- §9.3 — goSeq with peptide-count bias --------------------------------
# goSeq corrects ORA for the bias that proteins with more peptides are more
# easily detected as DE. We use peptide count per protein as the bias variable.

peptide_counts <- function(sum_obj) {
  sum_obj$FeatureLevelData %>%
    dplyr::distinct(ProteinName, PeptideSequence) %>%
    dplyr::count(ProteinName, name = "n_peptides") %>%
    dplyr::rename(Protein = ProteinName)
}
pitt_pep_n  <- peptide_counts(pitt_sum)
sheba_pep_n <- peptide_counts(sheba_sum)

goseq_pathway <- function(consensus, pw_map_obs, pep_n, mat_f, pathway_names,
                           label, direction = c("R_up","NR_up","Any")) {
  direction <- match.arg(direction)
  base <- consensus$tier1 | consensus$tier2
  if (direction == "R_up")  sig <- base & consensus$logFC_lim > 0
  if (direction == "NR_up") sig <- base & consensus$logFC_lim < 0
  if (direction == "Any")   sig <- base
  background <- rownames(mat_f)
  if (sum(sig & !is.na(sig)) < 5) {
    cat(label, " goSeq (", direction, "): too few sig — skipped\n", sep = ""); return(NULL)
  }

  de_vec <- setNames(as.integer(consensus$Protein %in% consensus$Protein[sig & !is.na(sig)]),
                     consensus$Protein)
  de_vec <- de_vec[names(de_vec) %in% background]
  bias <- pep_n$n_peptides[match(names(de_vec), pep_n$Protein)]
  bias[is.na(bias)] <- 1

  pwf <- tryCatch(goseq::nullp(de_vec, bias.data = bias, plot.fit = FALSE),
                  error = function(e) { cat(label,"nullp error:",e$message,"\n"); NULL })
  if (is.null(pwf)) return(NULL)

  cat2gene_list <- split(pw_map_obs$ProteinID, pw_map_obs$Pathway)
  res <- tryCatch(
    goseq::goseq(pwf, gene2cat = cat2gene_list, method = "Wallenius"),
    error = function(e) { cat(label,"goseq error:",e$message,"\n"); NULL }
  )
  if (is.null(res)) return(NULL)

  df <- res %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      Pathway = category,
      Name = pathway_names$Name[match(category, pathway_names$Pathway)],
      n_sig = numDEInCat,
      n_total = numInCat,
      p_goseq = over_represented_pvalue,
      direction = direction,
      cohort = label) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(p_goseq), n_total >= 3) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(q_goseq = p.adjust(p_goseq, method = "BH"))

  cat(label, " goSeq (", direction, "): ",
      sum(df$q_goseq < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " pathways at q<0.10, ",
      sum(df$p_goseq < 0.05, na.rm=TRUE), " at p<0.05\n", sep = "")
  df
}

pitt_goseq_R   <- goseq_pathway(pitt_consensus,  pitt_pw_map_obs,  pitt_pep_n,  pitt_mat_f,  kegg_pathway_names, "Pitt ", "R_up")
pitt_goseq_NR  <- goseq_pathway(pitt_consensus,  pitt_pw_map_obs,  pitt_pep_n,  pitt_mat_f,  kegg_pathway_names, "Pitt ", "NR_up")
sheba_goseq_R  <- goseq_pathway(sheba_consensus, sheba_pw_map_obs, sheba_pep_n, sheba_mat_f, kegg_pathway_names, "Sheba", "R_up")
sheba_goseq_NR <- goseq_pathway(sheba_consensus, sheba_pw_map_obs, sheba_pep_n, sheba_mat_f, kegg_pathway_names, "Sheba", "NR_up")
goseq_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(pitt_goseq_R, pitt_goseq_NR, sheba_goseq_R, sheba_goseq_NR)

# ---- §9.4 — Per-cohort consensus across ORA + GSEA + goSeq ----------------
# A pathway is "concordant" within a cohort if it reaches p<0.05 (or q<0.10)
# in ≥2 of {ORA, GSEA, goSeq} with consistent direction. This is the per-cohort
# substrate for §11–§13's combined-cohort verification gate.

build_pathway_consensus <- function(ora, gsea, goseq, label) {
  # Reduce to (Pathway, direction, cohort, p, q) per method then merge
  ora_l   <- ora   %>% dplyr::transmute(Pathway, Name, direction, p_ora,   q_ora)
  gsea_l  <- gsea  %>% dplyr::transmute(Pathway, Name, direction, p_gsea,  q_gsea)
  goseq_l <- goseq %>% dplyr::transmute(Pathway, Name, direction, p_goseq, q_goseq)

  d <- dplyr::full_join(ora_l, gsea_l,  by = c("Pathway","Name","direction")) %>%
       dplyr::full_join(goseq_l, by = c("Pathway","Name","direction")) %>%
       dplyr::mutate(
         n_p05 = (!is.na(p_ora)   & p_ora   < 0.05) +
                 (!is.na(p_gsea)  & p_gsea  < 0.05) +
                 (!is.na(p_goseq) & p_goseq < 0.05),
         n_q10 = (!is.na(q_ora)   & q_ora   < 0.10) +
                 (!is.na(q_gsea)  & q_gsea  < 0.10) +
                 (!is.na(q_goseq) & q_goseq < 0.10),
         cohort = label
       ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_q10), dplyr::desc(n_p05),
                   pmin(p_ora, p_gsea, p_goseq, na.rm = TRUE))

  cat("==== ", label, " pathway consensus ====\n", sep="")
  cat("  pathways with n_q10 >= 2: ", sum(d$n_q10 >= 2, na.rm=TRUE), "\n")
  cat("  pathways with n_p05 >= 2: ", sum(d$n_p05 >= 2, na.rm=TRUE), "\n")
  d
}

pitt_path_consensus  <- build_pathway_consensus(pitt_ora_R %>% dplyr::bind_rows(pitt_ora_NR),
                                                  pitt_gsea,
                                                  pitt_goseq_R %>% dplyr::bind_rows(pitt_goseq_NR),
                                                  "Pitt ")
sheba_path_consensus <- build_pathway_consensus(sheba_ora_R %>% dplyr::bind_rows(sheba_ora_NR),
                                                  sheba_gsea,
                                                  sheba_goseq_R %>% dplyr::bind_rows(sheba_goseq_NR),
                                                  "Sheba")

readr::write_csv(pitt_path_consensus,  file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "pitt_pathway_consensus.csv"))
readr::write_csv(sheba_path_consensus, file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "sheba_pathway_consensus.csv"))

options_old <- options(width = 220)

cat("==== Pitt top 15 pathways ====\n")
print(as.data.frame(
  pitt_path_consensus %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 15) %>%
    dplyr::select(Pathway, Name, direction, n_q10, n_p05,
                  p_ora, p_gsea, p_goseq)))

cat("\n==== Sheba top 15 pathways ====\n")
print(as.data.frame(
  sheba_path_consensus %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 15) %>%
    dplyr::select(Pathway, Name, direction, n_q10, n_p05,
                  p_ora, p_gsea, p_goseq)))

options(options_old)
```

## §9.5 — map00220 protein set

Collects the Pittsburgh proteins assigned to KEGG map00220. **It is kept
although the hypothesis that motivated it was dropped**, because it widens the
Unipept focus query in §10.1 and therefore determines which peptides went to
Unipept — so the frozen taxonomy caches the analysis reads were produced with
it in place. Removing it would narrow the query and make this document stop
reproducing those caches. It carries no claim of its own.

```{r h1_map00220_detail}
# All Pitt proteins assigned to map00220

  dplyr::filter(Pathway == "map00220") %>% dplyr::pull(ProteinID)
cat("Pitt proteins in map00220:", length(arg_proteins_pitt), "\n\n")
```

# §10 — Taxonomy via Unipept

Unipept LCA on tryptic peptides — the proteomic analog of MetaPhlAn taxonomic
profiling. This is **independent of the Prokka/eggNOG axis** because it
operates on amino-acid sequences directly, not protein IDs. So genus-level
counts are fully comparable across the two cohorts despite the disjoint
protein universes.

Genus-level verification requires nominal support (p<0.10) in both cohorts
with concordant direction.

## §10.1 — Submit peptides to Unipept

```{r unipept_helper}
# =============================================================================
# §10 — Unipept LCA taxonomy (focused queries)
# =============================================================================
# Unipept maps tryptic peptides → lowest-common-ancestor taxonomy across
# UniProt. Scientifically useful for assigning microbial protein hits to
# genus/species when the FASTA only has Prokka loci.
#
# Strategy:
#   §10.1 Build the "peptide → protein" maps for both cohorts from the
#         FeatureLevelData of the summarized objects.
#   §10.2 Query Unipept's pept2lca endpoint for the focus peptide sets:
#         - Pitt Tier 1+Tier 2 protein peptides
#         - Pitt map00220 protein peptides
#         - Sheba Tier 2 protein peptides
#   §10.3 LCA propagation: protein → set of LCAs (from peptides), pick the
#         consensus genus/species (most common at the deepest agreement level).
#   §10.4 Genus-level R-vs-NR consensus.
#
# Cache: Unipept queries are cached to disk to avoid re-querying on rerun.

library(httr2)
library(jsonlite)

UNIPEPT_CACHE <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "unipept_lca_cache.tsv")
UNIPEPT_BATCH <- 100   # Unipept rate limit: keep batches modest

# ---- §10.1 — Peptide → protein maps ---------------------------------------
build_peptide_map <- function(sum_obj, label) {
  pep_prot <- sum_obj$FeatureLevelData %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(PeptideSequence), !is.na(ProteinName)) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(ProteinName, PeptideSequence) %>%
    # Strip modifications: Unipept only takes plain amino acid sequences
    dplyr::mutate(PepClean = stringr::str_remove_all(PeptideSequence,
                                                      "[^A-Z]")) %>%
    dplyr::filter(nchar(PepClean) >= 5, nchar(PepClean) <= 50)  # Unipept limits
  cat(label, "— ", length(unique(pep_prot$PepClean)), " unique peptides across ",
      length(unique(pep_prot$ProteinName)), " proteins\n", sep="")
  pep_prot
}

pitt_pep_map  <- build_peptide_map(pitt_sum,  "Pitt ")
sheba_pep_map <- build_peptide_map(sheba_sum, "Sheba")

# ---- §10.2 — Unipept query (cached) ---------------------------------------
unipept_lookup <- function(peptides, cache_path = UNIPEPT_CACHE,
                            batch_size = UNIPEPT_BATCH) {
  peptides <- unique(peptides)

  cache <- if (file.exists(cache_path)) {
    readr::read_tsv(cache_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  } else {
    tibble::tibble(peptide = character(),
                   taxon_id = integer(), taxon_name = character(), taxon_rank = character(),
                   domain_name = character(), phylum_name = character(),
                   class_name = character(), order_name = character(),
                   family_name = character(), genus_name = character(),
                   species_name = character())
  }

  cached_peps <- intersect(peptides, cache$peptide)
  new_peps    <- setdiff(peptides, cached_peps)
  cat("Unipept: ", length(cached_peps), " cached, ", length(new_peps),
      " to query\n", sep="")
  if (length(new_peps) == 0) return(cache %>% dplyr::filter(peptide %in% peptides))

  results <- list()
  batches <- split(new_peps, ceiling(seq_along(new_peps) / batch_size))
  cat("Querying Unipept in ", length(batches), " batches of up to ",
      batch_size, " peptides ...\n", sep="")

  blank_to_na <- function(x) ifelse(is.character(x) & x == "", NA_character_, x)

  for (b_idx in seq_along(batches)) {
    b <- batches[[b_idx]]
    body <- c(stats::setNames(as.list(b), rep("input[]", length(b))),
              list(equate_il = "true", extra = "true", names = "true"))

    req <- httr2::request("https://api.unipept.ugent.be/api/v2/pept2lca.json") %>%
      httr2::req_method("POST") %>%
      httr2::req_body_form(!!!body) %>%
      httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 3, backoff = ~ 2 * .x) %>%
      httr2::req_throttle(rate = 5 / 1)

    resp <- tryCatch(httr2::req_perform(req),
                     error = function(e) {
                       cat("  batch ", b_idx, " ERROR: ", e$message, "\n", sep=""); NULL
                     })
    if (is.null(resp)) next

    json <- httr2::resp_body_json(resp, simplifyVector = TRUE)
    if (length(json) == 0 || (is.data.frame(json) && nrow(json) == 0)) next
    if (!is.data.frame(json)) json <- as.data.frame(json, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

    df <- tibble::tibble(
      peptide      = json$peptide,
      taxon_id     = json$taxon_id,
      taxon_name   = blank_to_na(json$taxon_name),
      taxon_rank   = blank_to_na(json$taxon_rank),
      domain_name  = blank_to_na(json$domain_name  %||% NA_character_),
      phylum_name  = blank_to_na(json$phylum_name  %||% NA_character_),
      class_name   = blank_to_na(json$class_name   %||% NA_character_),
      order_name   = blank_to_na(json$order_name   %||% NA_character_),
      family_name  = blank_to_na(json$family_name  %||% NA_character_),
      genus_name   = blank_to_na(json$genus_name   %||% NA_character_),
      species_name = blank_to_na(json$species_name %||% NA_character_)
    )
    results[[b_idx]] <- df

    if (b_idx %% 5 == 0)
      cat("  batch ", b_idx, "/", length(batches),
          " (", sum(sapply(results, nrow)), " peptides annotated)\n", sep="")
  }

  new_df <- if (length(results) > 0) do.call(rbind, results) else NULL
  if (is.null(new_df) || nrow(new_df) == 0) {
    cat("  no new annotations returned\n")
    return(cache %>% dplyr::filter(peptide %in% peptides))
  }

  unmatched <- setdiff(new_peps, new_df$peptide)
  if (length(unmatched) > 0) {
    new_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(new_df,
      tibble::tibble(peptide = unmatched,
                     taxon_id = NA_integer_, taxon_name = NA_character_,
                     taxon_rank = NA_character_, domain_name = NA_character_,
                     phylum_name = NA_character_, class_name = NA_character_,
                     order_name = NA_character_, family_name = NA_character_,
                     genus_name = NA_character_, species_name = NA_character_))
  }

  cache <- dplyr::bind_rows(cache, new_df) %>% dplyr::distinct(peptide, .keep_all = TRUE)
  readr::write_tsv(cache, cache_path)
  cache %>% dplyr::filter(peptide %in% peptides)
}

# Build the focus peptide set
focus_pitt_proteins <- unique(c(
  pitt_consensus$Protein[pitt_consensus$tier1 | pitt_consensus$tier2],
  arg_proteins_pitt    # all map00220 proteins
))
focus_pitt_peptides <- pitt_pep_map %>%
  dplyr::filter(ProteinName %in% focus_pitt_proteins) %>%
  dplyr::pull(PepClean)
cat("Pitt focus peptides: ", length(unique(focus_pitt_peptides)), "\n", sep="")

focus_sheba_proteins <- unique(sheba_consensus$Protein[
  sheba_consensus$tier1 | sheba_consensus$tier2])
focus_sheba_peptides <- sheba_pep_map %>%
  dplyr::filter(ProteinName %in% focus_sheba_proteins) %>%
  dplyr::pull(PepClean)
cat("Sheba focus peptides: ", length(unique(focus_sheba_peptides)), "\n", sep="")

# Run lookups
pitt_lca  <- unipept_lookup(focus_pitt_peptides)
sheba_lca <- unipept_lookup(focus_sheba_peptides)

cat("\nPitt  Unipept hits: ", sum(!is.na(pitt_lca$taxon_id)), "/",
    nrow(pitt_lca),  " peptides annotated\n", sep="")
cat("Sheba Unipept hits: ", sum(!is.na(sheba_lca$taxon_id)), "/",
    nrow(sheba_lca), " peptides annotated\n", sep="")
cat("\nPitt  rank distribution:\n"); print(table(pitt_lca$taxon_rank, useNA="ifany"))
cat("\nSheba rank distribution:\n"); print(table(sheba_lca$taxon_rank, useNA="ifany"))

# ---- §10.3 — Protein-level taxonomy from peptide LCA --------------------
protein_taxonomy <- function(pep_map, lca_table, label) {
  prot_tax <- pep_map %>%
    dplyr::left_join(lca_table %>% dplyr::select(peptide, taxon_name, taxon_rank,
                                                  genus_name, species_name,
                                                  domain_name),
                     by = c("PepClean" = "peptide"))
  per_prot <- prot_tax %>%
    dplyr::group_by(ProteinName) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      n_peps_total     = dplyr::n(),
      n_peps_annot     = sum(!is.na(taxon_name)),
      genus_consensus  = {
        g <- genus_name[!is.na(genus_name)]
        if (length(g) == 0) NA_character_ else names(sort(table(g), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
      },
      genus_consensus_pct = {
        g <- genus_name[!is.na(genus_name)]
        if (length(g) == 0) NA_real_ else max(table(g)) / length(g)
      },
      species_consensus = {
        s <- species_name[!is.na(species_name)]
        if (length(s) == 0) NA_character_ else names(sort(table(s), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
      },
      domain = {
        d <- domain_name[!is.na(domain_name)]
        if (length(d) == 0) NA_character_ else names(sort(table(d), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
      },
      .groups = "drop")
  cat(label, "— ", nrow(per_prot), " proteins with ≥1 peptide; genus consensus for ",
      sum(!is.na(per_prot$genus_consensus)), "\n", sep="")
  per_prot
}

pitt_prot_tax  <- protein_taxonomy(pitt_pep_map,  pitt_lca,  "Pitt ")
sheba_prot_tax <- protein_taxonomy(sheba_pep_map, sheba_lca, "Sheba")

# ---- §10.3a — Annotate Tier 1 with taxonomy -----------------------------
pitt_tier1_tax <- pitt_consensus %>%
  dplyr::filter(tier1) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    pitt_eggnog %>% dplyr::select(query, Preferred_name, KEGG_ko, Description) %>%
      dplyr::distinct(query, .keep_all = TRUE),
    by = c("Protein" = "query")) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(pitt_prot_tax, by = c("Protein" = "ProteinName")) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(q_lim) %>%
  dplyr::select(Protein, Preferred_name, logFC_lim, q_lim,
                genus_consensus, genus_consensus_pct, species_consensus,
                n_peps_annot)

cat("\n==== Pitt Tier 1 with Unipept taxonomy ====\n")
print(as.data.frame(pitt_tier1_tax))
readr::write_csv(pitt_tier1_tax,
                 file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "pitt_tier1_taxonomy.csv"))

# ---- §10.4 — Genus-level R-vs-NR consensus -----------------------------
# Aggregate protein-level logFC by genus (among proteins with a genus assignment)
# to get a genus-level direction summary. Two complementary aggregations:
#   (a) Mean logFC per genus weighted by 1/SE (limma)
#   (b) Sign test per genus (% of proteins NR-up)

genus_summary <- function(consensus, prot_tax, label, min_proteins = 3) {
  d <- consensus %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(logFC_lim), !is.na(p_lim)) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(prot_tax %>% dplyr::select(ProteinName, genus_consensus),
                     by = c("Protein" = "ProteinName")) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(genus_consensus))

  per_g <- d %>%
    dplyr::group_by(genus_consensus) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      n_proteins      = dplyr::n(),
      mean_logFC      = mean(logFC_lim),
      median_logFC    = median(logFC_lim),
      pct_NR_up       = mean(logFC_lim < 0) * 100,
      pct_R_up        = mean(logFC_lim > 0) * 100,
      sign_test_p     = if (dplyr::n() >= 3) {
        binom.test(sum(logFC_lim < 0), dplyr::n(), p = 0.5)$p.value
      } else NA_real_,
      .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::filter(n_proteins >= min_proteins) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(direction = ifelse(mean_logFC < 0, "NR_up", "R_up")) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(sign_test_p)

  cat("\n==== ", label, " genus-level summary (min ", min_proteins, " proteins) ====\n", sep="")
  cat("  ", nrow(per_g), " genera, ", sum(!is.na(per_g$sign_test_p) & per_g$sign_test_p < 0.05),
      " with sign-test p<0.05\n", sep="")
  print(as.data.frame(per_g %>% dplyr::slice_head(n = 25)))
  per_g
}

pitt_genus_summary  <- genus_summary(pitt_consensus,  pitt_prot_tax,  "Pitt ", 3)
sheba_genus_summary <- genus_summary(sheba_consensus, sheba_prot_tax, "Sheba", 3)

readr::write_csv(pitt_genus_summary,
                 file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "pitt_genus_consensus.csv"))
readr::write_csv(sheba_genus_summary,
                 file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "sheba_genus_consensus.csv"))

```

# =============================================================================
# §11 — Cross-cohort DA at three feature substrates
# =============================================================================
# Three parallel analyses:
#   §11.1 KEGG_Pathway-level (original H2 substrate, 151 well-covered pathways)
#   §11.2 KO-level           (denser than pathway, sparser than protein)
#   §11.3 Genus-level        (taxonomic, motivated by §10's Lachnospiraceae finding)
#
# Each uses median per-protein log-abundance per (sample, feature), then
# limma with: ~ 0 + Condition_bin + Cohort + Treatment_regimen
#
# Mixture is NOT included (as discussed: random unstratified plex assignment;
# Cohort-as-fixed absorbs the gross batch level).
```{r}
# ---- §11.0 — Build cross-cohort sample metadata ---------------------------
# Both cohorts share BioReplicate-keyed annotation. Build long-format meta.
build_combined_meta <- function() {
  pitt_meta <- pitt_annot_use %>%
    dplyr::filter(Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR")) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(Mixture, Channel, BioReplicate, Condition_bin,
                    Treatment_regimen, mg_overlap) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Sample = paste("Pitt", Mixture, Channel, sep = "_"),
                  Cohort = "Pitt")
  sheba_meta <- sheba_annot_use %>%
    dplyr::filter(Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR")) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(Mixture, Channel, BioReplicate, Condition_bin,
                    Treatment_regimen, mg_overlap) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Sample = paste("Sheba", Mixture, Channel, sep = "_"),
                  Cohort = "Sheba")
  dplyr::bind_rows(pitt_meta, sheba_meta) %>%
    dplyr::select(Sample, Cohort, BioReplicate, Mixture, Channel,
                  Condition_bin, Treatment_regimen, mg_overlap)
}
combined_meta <- build_combined_meta()
cat("Combined sample meta: ", nrow(combined_meta), " rows (",
    sum(combined_meta$Cohort == "Pitt"),  " Pitt + ",
    sum(combined_meta$Cohort == "Sheba"), " Sheba)\n", sep="")

# ---- §11.0a — Build long-format protein-by-sample table -----------------
# pitt_mat_f / sheba_mat_f have columns "Mixture_Channel" — prefix with Cohort
# to make samples globally unique.
build_long_table <- function(mat, label) {
  mat_renamed <- mat
  colnames(mat_renamed) <- paste(label, colnames(mat), sep = "_")
  long <- as.data.frame(mat_renamed) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Protein") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-Protein, names_to = "Sample", values_to = "logAbund") %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(logAbund)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Cohort = label)
  long
}
pitt_long  <- build_long_table(pitt_mat_f,  "Pitt")
sheba_long <- build_long_table(sheba_mat_f, "Sheba")

# ---- §11.0b — Median-aggregate to feature-level per sample --------------
# Generic aggregator: takes a Protein -> Feature map and produces a feature x
# sample matrix of median log-abundance across proteins assigned to that feature
# in that sample.
aggregate_to_feature <- function(long_tbl, feature_map, feature_col,
                                  min_proteins_per_feature_per_sample = 1) {
  long_with_feat <- long_tbl %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(feature_map, by = "Protein", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    dplyr::rename(Feature = !!feature_col)

  agg <- long_with_feat %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Feature, Sample) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(med_logAbund = median(logAbund),
                     n_proteins   = dplyr::n(),
                     .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::filter(n_proteins >= min_proteins_per_feature_per_sample)

  # Pivot to wide matrix
  wide <- agg %>%
    dplyr::select(Feature, Sample, med_logAbund) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Sample, values_from = med_logAbund)
  m <- as.matrix(wide[, -1])
  storage.mode(m) <- "double"
  rownames(m) <- wide$Feature
  m
}

# ---- §11.0c — Cross-cohort feature universe ------------------------------
# Pathway: 151 well-covered already in scope. Use intersection.
pathway_map_combined <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pitt_pw_map_obs  %>% dplyr::transmute(Protein = ProteinID, Pathway,
                                         Cohort = "Pitt"),
  sheba_pw_map_obs %>% dplyr::transmute(Protein = ProteinID, Pathway,
                                         Cohort = "Sheba")
)
# Restrict to well-covered intersection
pathway_map_use <- pathway_map_combined %>%
  dplyr::filter(Pathway %in% well_covered_pathways) %>%
  dplyr::select(Protein, Pathway)

# KO: intersection of Pitt + Sheba observed KOs, with min ≥3 proteins each
ko_universe_use <- intersect(unique(pitt_ko_map_obs$KO),
                              unique(sheba_ko_map_obs$KO))
ko_map_combined <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pitt_ko_map_obs  %>% dplyr::transmute(Protein = ProteinID, KO),
  sheba_ko_map_obs %>% dplyr::transmute(Protein = ProteinID, KO)
) %>%
  dplyr::filter(KO %in% ko_universe_use)

# Genus: intersection from §10b
genus_intersect <- intersect(pitt_genera, sheba_genera)
cat("Cross-cohort genus intersection: ", length(genus_intersect), "\n", sep="")
genus_map_combined <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pitt_prot_tax_full  %>% dplyr::transmute(Protein = ProteinName,
                                            Genus = genus_consensus),
  sheba_prot_tax_full %>% dplyr::transmute(Protein = ProteinName,
                                            Genus = genus_consensus)
) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Genus), Genus %in% genus_intersect)

# Combined long table
combined_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(pitt_long, sheba_long)

# Aggregate
pathway_mat <- aggregate_to_feature(combined_long,
                                     pathway_map_use,
                                     "Pathway",
                                     min_proteins_per_feature_per_sample = 3)
ko_mat      <- aggregate_to_feature(combined_long,
                                     ko_map_combined %>%
                                       dplyr::distinct(Protein, KO),
                                     "KO",
                                     min_proteins_per_feature_per_sample = 1)
genus_mat   <- aggregate_to_feature(combined_long,
                                     genus_map_combined %>%
                                       dplyr::distinct(Protein, Genus),
                                     "Genus",
                                     min_proteins_per_feature_per_sample = 3)

cat("\nFeature × sample matrices:\n")
cat("  Pathway:", nrow(pathway_mat), "x", ncol(pathway_mat),
    " missing =", round(100*mean(is.na(pathway_mat)), 1), "%\n")
cat("  KO     :", nrow(ko_mat),      "x", ncol(ko_mat),
    " missing =", round(100*mean(is.na(ko_mat)),      1), "%\n")
cat("  Genus  :", nrow(genus_mat),   "x", ncol(genus_mat),
    " missing =", round(100*mean(is.na(genus_mat)),   1), "%\n")

# ---- §11.1-3 — Cross-cohort limma DA per substrate -----------------------
combined_da <- function(mat, label) {
  # Subset metadata to matrix samples
  sm <- combined_meta %>% dplyr::filter(Sample %in% colnames(mat))
  mat <- mat[, sm$Sample, drop = FALSE]

  # Filter features with too much missingness across the combined set
  keep <- rowMeans(!is.na(mat)) >= 0.5
  mat  <- mat[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  cat(label, "— retained ", nrow(mat), " features after ≥50% detection filter\n", sep="")

  # Two model specs: primary (Cohort + Condition) and full (with Treatment_regimen)
  cond <- factor(sm$Condition_bin, levels = c("NR","R"))
  coh  <- factor(make.names(sm$Cohort))

  # Primary: ~ 0 + Condition + Cohort
  d1 <- model.matrix(~ 0 + cond + coh)
  colnames(d1) <- sub("^cond", "", colnames(d1))
  con1 <- limma::makeContrasts(R_vs_NR = R - NR, levels = d1)

  fit1  <- limma::lmFit(mat, d1)
  fit1b <- limma::eBayes(limma::contrasts.fit(fit1, con1), trend = TRUE, robust = TRUE)
  tt1   <- limma::topTable(fit1b, coef = "R_vs_NR", number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
  res_primary <- tibble::tibble(
    Feature = rownames(mat),
    logFC   = tt1$logFC, AveExpr = tt1$AveExpr,
    p_lim   = tt1$P.Value, q_lim = tt1$adj.P.Val)

  cat(label, "— primary (Condition + Cohort): ",
      sum(res_primary$q_lim < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " at q<0.10, ",
      sum(res_primary$p_lim < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " at p<0.10\n", sep="")

  # Sensitivity: + Treatment_regimen on mg_overlap subset only
  keep_meta <- !is.na(sm$Treatment_regimen)
  if (sum(keep_meta) >= 30) {
    sm2  <- sm[keep_meta, , drop = FALSE]
    mat2 <- mat[, sm2$Sample, drop = FALSE]
    cond2 <- factor(sm2$Condition_bin, levels = c("NR","R"))
    coh2 <- factor(make.names(sm2$Cohort))
    treat2 <- factor(make.names(sm2$Treatment_regimen))
    d2 <- model.matrix(~ 0 + cond2 + coh2 + treat2)
    colnames(d2) <- sub("^cond2", "", colnames(d2))
    con2 <- limma::makeContrasts(R_vs_NR = R - NR, levels = d2)
    fit2  <- limma::lmFit(mat2, d2)
    fit2b <- limma::eBayes(limma::contrasts.fit(fit2, con2), trend = TRUE, robust = TRUE)
    tt2   <- limma::topTable(fit2b, coef = "R_vs_NR", number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
    res_sens <- tibble::tibble(
      Feature = rownames(mat2),
      logFC_sens = tt2$logFC,
      p_sens     = tt2$P.Value,
      q_sens     = tt2$adj.P.Val)
    cat(label, "— sensitivity (+Treatment_regimen, n=", sum(keep_meta),
        "): ", sum(res_sens$q_sens < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " at q<0.10, ",
        sum(res_sens$p_sens < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE), " at p<0.10\n", sep="")
    res <- res_primary %>% dplyr::full_join(res_sens, by = "Feature")
  } else {
    res <- res_primary %>%
      dplyr::mutate(logFC_sens = NA_real_, p_sens = NA_real_, q_sens = NA_real_)
  }

  res %>% dplyr::arrange(p_lim)
}

cat("\n==== §11.1 KEGG_Pathway combined DA ====\n")
combined_pathway <- combined_da(pathway_mat, "Pathway")
combined_pathway <- combined_pathway %>%
  dplyr::left_join(kegg_pathway_names, by = c("Feature" = "Pathway")) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Pathway = Feature)
readr::write_csv(combined_pathway,
                 file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "combined_pathway_DA.csv"))

cat("\n==== §11.2 KO combined DA ====\n")
combined_ko <- combined_da(ko_mat, "KO")
readr::write_csv(combined_ko %>% dplyr::rename(KO = Feature),
                 file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "combined_KO_DA.csv"))

cat("\n==== §11.3 Genus combined DA ====\n")
combined_genus <- combined_da(genus_mat, "Genus")
readr::write_csv(combined_genus %>% dplyr::rename(Genus = Feature),
                 file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "combined_genus_DA.csv"))

# ---- Top-15 print per substrate -----------------------------------------
# NB: width capped at 140 (not 220) to avoid runaway verbatim blocks that
# can overflow pdflatex's main memory pool during knit-to-PDF.
opt <- options(width = 140)
cat("\n==== Combined Pathway DA — top 20 ====\n")
print(as.data.frame(combined_pathway %>%
        dplyr::slice_head(n = 20) %>%
        dplyr::select(Pathway, Name, logFC, p_lim, q_lim, logFC_sens, p_sens, q_sens)))

cat("\n==== Combined KO DA — top 20 ====\n")
print(as.data.frame(combined_ko %>%
        dplyr::slice_head(n = 20) %>%
        dplyr::select(Feature, logFC, p_lim, q_lim, logFC_sens, p_sens, q_sens)))

cat("\n==== Combined Genus DA — top 30 (full table in CSV) ====\n")
print(as.data.frame(combined_genus %>%
        dplyr::slice_head(n = 30) %>%
        dplyr::select(Feature, logFC, p_lim, q_lim, logFC_sens, p_sens, q_sens)))
options(opt)

# ---- §11.4 — Save state for §13 / §14 -----------------------------------
saveRDS(list(
  pitt_consensus       = pitt_consensus,
  sheba_consensus      = sheba_consensus,
  pitt_prot_tax_full   = pitt_prot_tax_full,
  sheba_prot_tax_full  = sheba_prot_tax_full,
  pitt_genus_summary   = pitt_genus_summary,
  sheba_genus_summary  = sheba_genus_summary,
  combined_pathway     = combined_pathway,
  combined_ko          = combined_ko,
  combined_genus       = combined_genus,
  pitt_path_consensus  = pitt_path_consensus,
  sheba_path_consensus = sheba_path_consensus,
  combined_meta        = combined_meta,
  pathway_mat          = pathway_mat,
  ko_mat               = ko_mat,
  genus_mat            = genus_mat
), file.path(OUT_DIR, "metaproteomics_post11.rds"))
cat("\nSaved checkpoint: metaproteomics_post11.rds\n")
```

## §11.5 — Data-based eligibility re-filter (`_xx` substrate)

The §11.0c eligibility filters used the *annotation* universe — proteins that
COULD have a KO/Pathway according to eggNOG. But the actual cross-cohort
substrate must use proteins that have ACTUAL DATA in `combined_long` after
the §4 detection filter. This chunk re-filters at the data level, requiring
≥3 quantified proteins per cohort per feature.

This produces the `_xx` matrices that are used in the §13 verification gate
and §14 verdict tables. The XX vs base difference is the right one — only
features with genuine cross-cohort information content.

```{r combined_da_xx}
# ---- §11.5a — Build (Protein × Cohort) "with-data" map -----------------
proteins_with_data <- combined_long %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Protein, Cohort)
cat("Proteins with data: ",
    sum(proteins_with_data$Cohort == "Pitt"),  " Pitt + ",
    sum(proteins_with_data$Cohort == "Sheba"), " Sheba\n", sep="")

# ---- §11.5b — Per-feature cohort coverage ------------------------------
# KO eligibility
ko_map_data_tagged <- ko_map_combined %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Protein, KO) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(proteins_with_data, by = "Protein")
ko_cohort_coverage <- ko_map_data_tagged %>%
  dplyr::group_by(KO, Cohort) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n_prot = dplyr::n_distinct(Protein), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Cohort, values_from = n_prot, values_fill = 0)
ko_cross_eligible_v2 <- ko_cohort_coverage %>%
  dplyr::filter(Pitt >= 3, Sheba >= 3) %>% dplyr::pull(KO)

# Pathway eligibility
pathway_map_data_tagged <- pathway_map_combined %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Protein, Pathway) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(proteins_with_data, by = "Protein")
pathway_cohort_coverage <- pathway_map_data_tagged %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Pathway, Cohort) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n_prot = dplyr::n_distinct(Protein), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Cohort, values_from = n_prot, values_fill = 0)
pathway_cross_eligible_v2 <- pathway_cohort_coverage %>%
  dplyr::filter(Pitt >= 3, Sheba >= 3) %>% dplyr::pull(Pathway)

# Genus eligibility
genus_map_data_tagged <- genus_map_combined %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Protein, Genus) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(proteins_with_data, by = "Protein")
genus_cohort_coverage <- genus_map_data_tagged %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Genus, Cohort) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n_prot = dplyr::n_distinct(Protein), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Cohort, values_from = n_prot, values_fill = 0)
genus_cross_eligible_v2 <- genus_cohort_coverage %>%
  dplyr::filter(Pitt >= 3, Sheba >= 3) %>% dplyr::pull(Genus)

cat("\n==== Data-based eligibility (≥3 proteins per cohort) ====\n")
cat("KO:       ", length(ko_cross_eligible_v2),      " / ",
    nrow(ko_cohort_coverage),      " annotated\n", sep="")
cat("Pathway:  ", length(pathway_cross_eligible_v2), " / ",
    nrow(pathway_cohort_coverage), " annotated\n", sep="")
cat("Genus:    ", length(genus_cross_eligible_v2),   " / ",
    nrow(genus_cohort_coverage),   " annotated\n", sep="")

# ---- §11.5c — Subset matrices and re-run combined_da ----------------------
ko_mat_xx      <- ko_mat[rownames(ko_mat) %in% ko_cross_eligible_v2,, drop=FALSE]
pathway_mat_xx <- pathway_mat[rownames(pathway_mat) %in% pathway_cross_eligible_v2,, drop=FALSE]
genus_mat_xx   <- genus_mat[rownames(genus_mat) %in% genus_cross_eligible_v2,, drop=FALSE]

cat("\n==== §11.5 Data-eligibility XX matrices ====\n")
cat("KO_xx:       ", nrow(ko_mat_xx),      " features × ", ncol(ko_mat_xx),      " samples\n", sep="")
cat("Pathway_xx:  ", nrow(pathway_mat_xx), " features × ", ncol(pathway_mat_xx), " samples\n", sep="")
cat("Genus_xx:    ", nrow(genus_mat_xx),   " features × ", ncol(genus_mat_xx),   " samples\n", sep="")

cat("\n==== §11.5d KEGG_Pathway combined DA (XX) ====\n")
combined_pathway_xx <- combined_da(pathway_mat_xx, "Pathway-XX") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(kegg_pathway_names, by = c("Feature" = "Pathway"))

cat("\n==== §11.5e KO combined DA (XX) ====\n")
combined_ko_xx <- combined_da(ko_mat_xx, "KO-XX")

cat("\n==== §11.5f Genus combined DA (XX) ====\n")
combined_genus_xx <- combined_da(genus_mat_xx, "Genus-XX")
```

## §11.6 — Tier construction + microbial pathway filter

Defines the headline tier columns used in §13 / §14:
- `Tier1_primary`: combined q<0.10 in primary model
- `Tier1_robust`:  q<0.10 in BOTH primary AND sensitivity (+Treatment_regimen)
- `Tier2_robust`:  q<0.10 primary + p<0.10 sensitivity (publication-grade subset)
- `Tier1_kegg_microbial`: Tier1_primary AND not in known host-cross-mapping
  artifacts (map04*, map05*, umbrella maps map01100/01200/01220)

```{r tier_construction}
# Microbial pathway filter — exclude known host-cross-mapping artifacts
host_artifact_pathways <- c(
  "map01100",  # "Metabolic pathways" umbrella
  "map01200",  # "Carbon metabolism" umbrella
  "map01220"   # "Degradation of aromatic compounds" umbrella
)
is_microbial_pathway <- function(pw_id) {
  m <- as.integer(sub("^map", "", pw_id))
  is_host <- (m >= 4000 & m < 5500) | pw_id %in% host_artifact_pathways
  !is_host
}

combined_pathway_xx <- combined_pathway_xx %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Tier1_primary        = !is.na(q_lim)  & q_lim  < 0.10,
    Tier1_robust         = !is.na(q_lim)  & q_lim  < 0.10 &
                           !is.na(q_sens) & q_sens < 0.10,
    Tier2_robust         = !is.na(q_lim)  & q_lim  < 0.10 &
                           !is.na(p_sens) & p_sens < 0.10,
    Tier1_kegg_microbial = (!is.na(q_lim) & q_lim < 0.10) &
                           is_microbial_pathway(Feature)
  )

combined_ko_xx <- combined_ko_xx %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Tier1_primary = !is.na(q_lim) & q_lim < 0.10,
    Tier1_robust  = !is.na(q_lim) & q_lim < 0.10 & !is.na(q_sens) & q_sens < 0.10,
    Tier2_robust  = !is.na(q_lim) & q_lim < 0.10 & !is.na(p_sens) & p_sens < 0.10
  )

combined_genus_xx <- combined_genus_xx %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Tier1_primary = !is.na(q_lim) & q_lim < 0.10,
    Tier1_robust  = !is.na(q_lim) & q_lim < 0.10 & !is.na(q_sens) & q_sens < 0.10,
    Tier2_robust  = !is.na(q_lim) & q_lim < 0.10 & !is.na(p_sens) & p_sens < 0.10
  )

cat("==== Final cross-cohort tiers (XX substrate) ====\n")
cat("Pathway Tier1_primary:        ", sum(combined_pathway_xx$Tier1_primary, na.rm=TRUE), "\n")
cat("Pathway Tier1_kegg_microbial: ", sum(combined_pathway_xx$Tier1_kegg_microbial, na.rm=TRUE), "\n")
cat("Pathway Tier1_robust:         ", sum(combined_pathway_xx$Tier1_robust, na.rm=TRUE), "\n")
cat("Pathway Tier2_robust:         ", sum(combined_pathway_xx$Tier2_robust, na.rm=TRUE), "\n")
cat("KO      Tier1_primary:        ", sum(combined_ko_xx$Tier1_primary, na.rm=TRUE), "\n")
cat("KO      Tier2_robust:         ", sum(combined_ko_xx$Tier2_robust, na.rm=TRUE), "\n")
cat("Genus   Tier1_primary:        ", sum(combined_genus_xx$Tier1_primary, na.rm=TRUE), "\n")

# ---- Tier 2 robust pathway summary table — publication-grade -------------
cat("\n==== Tier 2 robust pathways (publication-grade hits) ====\n")
tier2_robust_table <- combined_pathway_xx %>%
  dplyr::filter(Tier2_robust) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(p_lim) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(Feature, Name, logFC, q_lim, logFC_sens, p_sens,
                   microbial = Tier1_kegg_microbial)
print(as.data.frame(tier2_robust_table))
readr::write_csv(tier2_robust_table,
                 file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "combined_pathway_tier2_robust.csv"))
readr::write_csv(combined_pathway_xx,
                 file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "combined_pathway_xx.csv"))
readr::write_csv(combined_ko_xx,
                 file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "combined_KO_xx.csv"))
readr::write_csv(combined_genus_xx,
                 file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "combined_genus_xx.csv"))
```

## §11.7 — K03695/K03696 ClpB/ClpC chaperone audit

A pre-XX run flagged K03695 (ClpB) and K03696 (ClpC) as q<0.10 NR-up cross-cohort.
Investigation showed eggNOG bundles them as a degenerate orthology pair AND
the §50% detection filter retains only 2 of 22 ClpB/ClpC proteins in Pitt and
0 in Sheba. The cross-cohort signal is therefore Pitt-driven by 2 proteins,
not a genuine cross-cohort finding.

This chunk documents that audit so future readers don't reanimate K03695/K03696
as a cross-cohort hit.

```{r clpB_clpC_audit}
clp_KOs <- c("K03695","K03696")  # ClpB, ClpC

# How many proteins map to these KOs in each cohort's eggNOG?
clp_pitt  <- pitt_ko_map_obs  %>% dplyr::filter(KO %in% clp_KOs) %>% dplyr::pull(ProteinID) %>% unique()
clp_sheba <- sheba_ko_map_obs %>% dplyr::filter(KO %in% clp_KOs) %>% dplyr::pull(ProteinID) %>% unique()
cat("Pitt  ClpB/ClpC-annotated microbial proteins (any detection): ",
    length(clp_pitt),  "\n", sep="")
cat("Sheba ClpB/ClpC-annotated microbial proteins (any detection): ",
    length(clp_sheba), "\n", sep="")

# How many survive the §4 ≥50% detection filter?
clp_pitt_survived  <- intersect(clp_pitt,  rownames(pitt_mat_f))
clp_sheba_survived <- intersect(clp_sheba, rownames(sheba_mat_f))
cat("Pitt  ClpB/ClpC after ≥50% detection filter: ",
    length(clp_pitt_survived),  "\n", sep="")
cat("Sheba ClpB/ClpC after ≥50% detection filter: ",
    length(clp_sheba_survived), "\n", sep="")

# Pitt-level effect on the surviving proteins
if (length(clp_pitt_survived) > 0) {
  pitt_clp_da <- pitt_consensus %>%
    dplyr::filter(Protein %in% clp_pitt_survived) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      pitt_eggnog %>% dplyr::select(query, Preferred_name, KEGG_ko) %>%
        dplyr::distinct(query, .keep_all = TRUE),
      by = c("Protein" = "query")) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(p_lim)
  cat("\n==== Pitt ClpB/ClpC DA (surviving filter) ====\n")
  print(as.data.frame(pitt_clp_da %>%
          dplyr::select(Protein, Preferred_name, KEGG_ko,
                        logFC_lim, p_lim, q_lim, tier1)))
}

cat("\nK03695/K03696 cross-cohort signal is Pittsburgh-only; it is not\n")
cat("carried into the manuscript.\n")
```

## §11.8 — Combined-cohort GSEA on ranked KO substrate

Independent test of the §11.5 limma-on-aggregated-medians approach. Uses the
ranked KO list from `combined_ko_xx` (signed logFC × -log10(p)), maps KOs to
KEGG pathways via cross-cohort eggNOG, runs `clusterProfiler::GSEA`. A
pathway passing both combined limma q<0.10 AND combined GSEA p<0.10 is
strong cross-cohort evidence.

```{r combined_gsea}
# Build cross-cohort KO -> Pathway map
ko_to_pathway <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    pitt_eggnog %>% dplyr::select(KEGG_ko, KEGG_Pathway),
    sheba_eggnog %>% dplyr::select(KEGG_ko, KEGG_Pathway)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(KEGG_ko), !is.na(KEGG_Pathway)) %>%
  tidyr::separate_rows(KEGG_ko, sep = ",") %>%
  tidyr::separate_rows(KEGG_Pathway, sep = ",") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(KO = stringr::str_remove(KEGG_ko, "^ko:"),
                Pathway = stringr::str_replace(KEGG_Pathway, "^ko", "map")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(Pathway, "^map\\d+")) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Pathway, KO)

# Rank vector from combined_ko_xx
ranks_combined <- combined_ko_xx %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(logFC), !is.na(p_lim)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(score = sign(logFC) * -log10(p_lim)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(score))
rank_vec_combined <- setNames(ranks_combined$score, ranks_combined$Feature)

cat("Combined-cohort GSEA: ", length(rank_vec_combined),
    " KOs ranked, mapped to ", dplyr::n_distinct(ko_to_pathway$Pathway),
    " pathways\n", sep="")

combined_gsea_pathway <- tryCatch(
  clusterProfiler::GSEA(
    geneList = rank_vec_combined,
    TERM2GENE = ko_to_pathway %>% dplyr::select(Pathway, KO),
    TERM2NAME = kegg_pathway_names,
    pvalueCutoff = 1, minGSSize = 5, maxGSSize = 500, eps = 0,
    seed = TRUE, verbose = FALSE),
  error = function(e) {cat("GSEA error:", e$message, "\n"); NULL})

if (!is.null(combined_gsea_pathway) &&
    nrow(as.data.frame(combined_gsea_pathway)) > 0) {
  combined_gsea_pathway_df <- as.data.frame(combined_gsea_pathway) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(Pathway = ID, Name = Description, NES,
                     p_gsea_comb = pvalue, q_gsea_comb = p.adjust,
                     direction = ifelse(NES > 0, "R_up", "NR_up")) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(p_gsea_comb)
  cat("\nCombined GSEA: ",
      sum(combined_gsea_pathway_df$q_gsea_comb < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE),
      " pathways at q<0.10, ",
      sum(combined_gsea_pathway_df$p_gsea_comb < 0.05, na.rm=TRUE),
      " at p<0.05\n", sep="")
  cat("\n==== Top 15 combined-cohort GSEA hits ====\n")
  print(as.data.frame(combined_gsea_pathway_df %>% dplyr::slice_head(n = 15)))
  readr::write_csv(combined_gsea_pathway_df,
                   file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "combined_gsea_pathway.csv"))
} else {
  combined_gsea_pathway_df <- NULL
  cat("Combined GSEA returned no enrichment.\n")
}
```

## §11.9 — Combined-cohort PERMANOVA at the pathway level

Activity-level β-diversity analog of the metagenomic combined PERMANOVA
(metagenomics: Cohort R²=39%, Condition R²=0.6%, p=0.97). If pathway-level
metaproteomic Condition R² > 1%, that's a clean visual H2 result — composition
β-diversity didn't see Response, activity β-diversity does.

```{r combined_pathway_permanova}
# Use complete-case pathway_mat (XX-filtered or not — use full for max signal,
# subset to samples with Treatment_regimen for the sensitivity test)
mat_pw <- pathway_mat_xx
mat_complete <- mat_pw[complete.cases(mat_pw), , drop = FALSE]
sm_pw <- combined_meta %>%
  dplyr::filter(Sample %in% colnames(mat_complete))
mat_complete <- mat_complete[, sm_pw$Sample, drop = FALSE]

if (ncol(mat_complete) >= 30 && nrow(mat_complete) >= 20) {
  cat("==== Combined-cohort pathway-level PERMANOVA (primary) ====\n")
  cat("  features:", nrow(mat_complete), "  samples:", ncol(mat_complete), "\n")
  permanova_pw_combined <- vegan::adonis2(
    t(mat_complete) ~ Cohort + Condition_bin,
    data = sm_pw, by = "margin", permutations = 999)
  print(permanova_pw_combined)

  # Sensitivity: + Treatment_regimen on mg_overlap subset
  sm_pw_sens <- sm_pw %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(Treatment_regimen))
  if (nrow(sm_pw_sens) >= 30) {
    mat_sens <- mat_complete[, sm_pw_sens$Sample, drop = FALSE]
    cat("\n==== Combined PERMANOVA (sensitivity: +Treatment_regimen) ====\n")
    cat("  samples:", ncol(mat_sens), "\n")
    permanova_pw_combined_sens <- vegan::adonis2(
      t(mat_sens) ~ Cohort + Condition_bin + Treatment_regimen,
      data = sm_pw_sens, by = "margin", permutations = 999)
    print(permanova_pw_combined_sens)
  } else {
    permanova_pw_combined_sens <- NULL
  }
} else {
  cat("Too few complete-case features/samples for combined PERMANOVA\n")
  permanova_pw_combined <- NULL
  permanova_pw_combined_sens <- NULL
}
```
# =============================================================================
# §16 — Cross-omic anti-correlation figure
# =============================================================================
# The cleanest visual H2 / H3 result: are composition-level (metagenomic) and
# activity-level (metaproteomic) signals correlated, anti-correlated, or
# independent? Two panels:
#   (a) Pathway-level scatter (where mg_state has KEGG-level pathway results)
#   (b) Genus-level scatter (using Unipept genera that intersect mg_state genera)
#
# Annotated with the Lachnospiraceae genera. If correlation is near 0, the
# "composition does not predict activity" framing is supported visually.

```{r cross_omic_scatter}
# ---- §16a Pathway-level cross-omic scatter ------------------------------
# Metagenomic pathway results are MetaCyc IDs in mg_state; metaproteomic are
# KEGG map IDs. We attempt a name-based join — imperfect but informative.
# If mg_state$path_combo has KEGG-mapped results, use those directly.

pathway_xomic_plot <- NULL
genus_xomic_plot   <- NULL

if (!is.null(mg_state) && !is.null(mg_state$path_combo)) {
  # Attempt KEGG-level metagenomic pathway results
  mg_path <- tryCatch(
    mg_state$path_combo %>%
      tibble::as_tibble() %>%
      dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(c("Pathway", "Feature", "logFC",
                                     "padj", "Name", "name"))),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (!is.null(mg_path) && nrow(mg_path) > 0) {
    # Try a name-based join (KEGG names like "Nitrogen metabolism" should
    # match MetaCyc names approximately)
    mp_path <- combined_pathway_xx %>%
      dplyr::filter(Tier1_kegg_microbial) %>%
      dplyr::select(Pathway = Feature, Name, mp_logFC = logFC,
                    mp_q = q_lim, microbial = Tier1_kegg_microbial)

    cat("Cross-omic pathway scatter: (will skip if no shared IDs found)\n")
    cat("  metagenomic pathway records: ", nrow(mg_path),  "\n")
    cat("  metaproteomic pathway hits : ", nrow(mp_path),  "\n")

    # If there's a Pathway column in mg_path, do an ID-based join
    if ("Pathway" %in% colnames(mg_path)) {
      xomic_path <- mp_path %>%
        dplyr::inner_join(mg_path %>%
                            dplyr::transmute(Pathway, mg_logFC = logFC),
                          by = "Pathway")
      if (nrow(xomic_path) >= 3) {
        cat("  ID-matched pairs: ", nrow(xomic_path), "\n")
        pathway_xomic_plot <- ggplot(xomic_path,
            aes(x = mg_logFC, y = mp_logFC, label = Name)) +
          geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
          geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
          geom_point(size = 2.5, colour = "#1f78b4", alpha = 0.85) +
          ggrepel::geom_text_repel(size = 2.6, max.overlaps = 25,
                                    box.padding = 0.4,
                                    segment.colour = "grey70") +
          labs(title = "Cross-omic pathway logFC",
               subtitle = paste0("KEGG-pathway-matched, n=", nrow(xomic_path)),
               x = "Metagenomic logFC (R - NR)",
               y = "Metaproteomic logFC (R - NR)") +
          theme_bw(base_size = 11)
        ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "figures", "xomic_pathway_scatter.png"),
               pathway_xomic_plot, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 150)
      }
    }
  }
}

# ---- §16b Genus-level cross-omic scatter --------------------------------
if (!is.null(mg_state) && !is.null(mg_state$combo_genus)) {
  mg_genus <- tryCatch(
    {
      g <- mg_state$combo_genus
      if (methods::is(g, "data.frame") || tibble::is_tibble(g)) {
        g %>% tibble::as_tibble() %>%
          dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(c("Genus","Feature","Taxon",
                                         "logFC","mg_logFC")))
      } else NULL
    },
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (!is.null(mg_genus) && nrow(mg_genus) > 0) {
    # Standardize column names
    if ("Feature" %in% colnames(mg_genus) && !"Genus" %in% colnames(mg_genus))
      mg_genus <- mg_genus %>% dplyr::rename(Genus = Feature)
    if ("Taxon" %in% colnames(mg_genus) && !"Genus" %in% colnames(mg_genus))
      mg_genus <- mg_genus %>% dplyr::rename(Genus = Taxon)
    if ("logFC" %in% colnames(mg_genus) && !"mg_logFC" %in% colnames(mg_genus))
      mg_genus <- mg_genus %>% dplyr::rename(mg_logFC = logFC)

    if (all(c("Genus","mg_logFC") %in% colnames(mg_genus))) {
      mp_genus <- combined_genus_xx %>%
        dplyr::transmute(Genus = Feature, mp_logFC = logFC, mp_p = p_lim)
      xomic_g <- mp_genus %>%
        dplyr::inner_join(mg_genus %>%
                            dplyr::distinct(Genus, mg_logFC),
                          by = "Genus")

      if (nrow(xomic_g) >= 3) {
        cat("\nCross-omic genus scatter pairs: ", nrow(xomic_g), "\n")
        cor_g <- cor.test(xomic_g$mg_logFC, xomic_g$mp_logFC)
        cat("Spearman correlation: r =", round(cor_g$estimate,2),
            ", p =", round(cor_g$p.value, 3), "\n")

        genus_xomic_plot <- ggplot(xomic_g,
              aes(x = mg_logFC, y = mp_logFC, label = Genus)) +
          geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
          geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
          geom_point(size = 2.5, colour = "#33a02c", alpha = 0.85) +
          ggrepel::geom_text_repel(size = 2.6, max.overlaps = 25,
                                    box.padding = 0.4,
                                    segment.colour = "grey70") +
          labs(title = "Cross-omic genus logFC",
               subtitle = paste0("Genus-matched, n=", nrow(xomic_g),
                                 ", r=", round(cor_g$estimate,2)),
               x = "Metagenomic logFC (R - NR)",
               y = "Metaproteomic logFC (R - NR)") +
          theme_bw(base_size = 11)
        ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "figures", "xomic_genus_scatter.png"),
               genus_xomic_plot, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 150)
      }
    }
  }
}

# Combine if both made
if (!is.null(pathway_xomic_plot) && !is.null(genus_xomic_plot)) {
  p_xomic <- pathway_xomic_plot + genus_xomic_plot +
    patchwork::plot_layout(ncol = 2)
  ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "figures", "xomic_combined_scatter.png"),
         p_xomic, width = 13, height = 6, dpi = 150)
  print(p_xomic)
} else if (!is.null(pathway_xomic_plot)) {
  print(pathway_xomic_plot)
} else if (!is.null(genus_xomic_plot)) {
  print(genus_xomic_plot)
} else {
  warning("§16 cross-omic scatter not generated — neither mg_state$path_combo ",
          "nor mg_state$combo_genus produced a usable joinable column structure. ",
          "Check colnames(mg_state$path_combo) and colnames(mg_state$combo_genus); ",
          "the chunk attempts to detect Pathway/Feature/Taxon/Name + logFC columns ",
          "and falls through if none match.")
  cat("[§16] Cross-omic scatter SKIPPED — see warning() output for diagnostics.\n")
}
```

# =============================================================================
# §17 — Sheba power analysis
# =============================================================================
# Sheba had 0 Tier 1 hits at q<0.10. Reviewers will ask: "is that biology
# (no signal) or sample size (n=11 NR underpowered)?" This computes the
# Bonferroni-corrected detectable effect size at Sheba's n=30 R / n=11 NR
# and compares to the median Pitt Tier 1 effect size.

```{r sheba_power}
if (requireNamespace("pwr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  n_R_sheba  <- 30
  n_NR_sheba <- 11
  n_tests    <- nrow(sheba_mat_f)
  alpha_corr <- 0.05 / n_tests   # Bonferroni

  # Pooled SD across Sheba proteins (median)
  if (requireNamespace("matrixStats", quietly = TRUE)) {
    sd_pool_sheba <- median(matrixStats::rowSds(sheba_mat_f, na.rm = TRUE),
                             na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    sd_pool_sheba <- median(apply(sheba_mat_f, 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  power_d <- tryCatch(
    pwr::pwr.t2n.test(n1 = n_R_sheba, n2 = n_NR_sheba,
                       sig.level = alpha_corr, power = 0.8)$d,
    error = function(e) NA_real_)
  power_d_uncorr <- tryCatch(
    pwr::pwr.t2n.test(n1 = n_R_sheba, n2 = n_NR_sheba,
                       sig.level = 0.05, power = 0.8)$d,
    error = function(e) NA_real_)

  # Median Pitt Tier 1 effect size for comparison
  pitt_t1_logFC <- median(abs(pitt_consensus$logFC_lim[
    pitt_consensus$tier1 & !is.na(pitt_consensus$logFC_lim)]))

  cat("==== Sheba power analysis ====\n")
  cat("n_R = ", n_R_sheba, ", n_NR = ", n_NR_sheba,
      ", n_tests = ", n_tests, "\n", sep="")
  cat("Pooled SD (median across proteins): ", round(sd_pool_sheba, 2), " log2\n", sep="")
  cat("Bonferroni-corrected α = ", signif(alpha_corr, 2), "\n", sep="")
  cat("Detectable Cohen's d at 80% power (Bonferroni): ",
      round(power_d, 2), "\n", sep="")
  cat("  → equivalent logFC: ", round(power_d * sd_pool_sheba, 2), "\n", sep="")
  cat("Detectable Cohen's d at 80% power (uncorrected): ",
      round(power_d_uncorr, 2), "\n", sep="")
  cat("  → equivalent logFC: ", round(power_d_uncorr * sd_pool_sheba, 2), "\n", sep="")
  cat("Median |logFC| of Pitt Tier 1 hits: ",
      round(pitt_t1_logFC, 2), " log2\n", sep="")

  sheba_power <- list(
    n_R = n_R_sheba, n_NR = n_NR_sheba, n_tests = n_tests,
    alpha_bonferroni = alpha_corr,
    detectable_cohen_d_corrected   = power_d,
    detectable_cohen_d_uncorrected = power_d_uncorr,
    detectable_logFC_corrected     = power_d * sd_pool_sheba,
    detectable_logFC_uncorrected   = power_d_uncorr * sd_pool_sheba,
    pitt_tier1_median_abs_logFC    = pitt_t1_logFC
  )
} else {
  cat("pwr package not installed — skipping Sheba power analysis\n")
  sheba_power <- NULL
}
```
# =============================================================================
# §18 — Host protein analysis (exploratory)
# =============================================================================
#
# Rationale: §1.4.3 split the FragPipe output into microbial (§3-§17) and host
# (`pitt_raw_host` / `sheba_raw_host`, never analyzed). Pitt has 577 host
# SwissProt + 6 TrEMBL proteins; Sheba has 355 + 3. Unlike microbial proteins,
# host IDs are shared UniProt accessions across cohorts, so cross-cohort runs
# at protein-level directly — no KO/Pathway aggregation needed.
#
# Framing: EXPLORATORY. No pre-registered hypothesis. We're scanning the host
# axis to see whether anything jumps out (gut-barrier, immune, inflammation
# markers being the prior on what's quantifiable in stool). No verification gate.
#
# Pipeline (2-method consensus, simpler than §7's 3-method):
#   §18.1 Summarize host proteins via MSstatsTMT, build matrices, ≥50% filter
#   §18.2 PCA + PERMANOVA per cohort
#   §18.3 Per-cohort DA: limma + permutation
#   §18.4 Cross-cohort meta-analysis (Stouffer's, protein-level)
#   §18.5 Enrichment: goSeq GO:BP + GSEA on MSigDB Hallmarks
#   §18.6 Targeted lookups: stool host marker panel
#   §18.7 Cross-omic with mg_state pathways / genera

## §18.0 — Setup: optional packages, identifier cleanup
```{r host_setup}
# Optional packages — don't fail the chunk if unavailable, just skip the
# downstream subsections that need them.
HOST_HAS_ENSDB   <- requireNamespace("EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86", quietly = TRUE) &&
                    requireNamespace("ensembldb",         quietly = TRUE)
HOST_HAS_MSIGDBR <- requireNamespace("msigdbr",           quietly = TRUE)
HOST_HAS_GOSEQ   <- requireNamespace("goseq",             quietly = TRUE)

cat("Optional packages for §18:\n")
cat("  EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86 + ensembldb : ", HOST_HAS_ENSDB,   "\n")
cat("  msigdbr                        : ", HOST_HAS_MSIGDBR, "\n")
cat("  goseq                          : ", HOST_HAS_GOSEQ,   "\n")

# Identifier cleanup: FragPipe headers look like `sp|P12345|GENE_HUMAN` or
# `tr|A0A024R5K0|A0A024R5K0_HUMAN`. We want the gene symbol for enrichment
# (after stripping `_HUMAN`) and the UniProt accession for cross-cohort joins.
parse_host_id <- function(x) {
  parts <- stringr::str_split_fixed(x, "\\|", n = 3)
  uniprot   <- parts[, 2]
  gene_long <- parts[, 3]
  gene      <- stringr::str_remove(gene_long, "_HUMAN.*$")
  # Some TrEMBL entries have the accession in position 3 too (no gene symbol).
  # In that case keep the UniProt accession as the "gene" for downstream joins.
  gene <- ifelse(gene == "" | gene == uniprot, uniprot, gene)
  tibble::tibble(ProteinName = x, UniProt = uniprot, Gene = gene)
}

# Sanity: confirm host objects exist from §1.4.3
stopifnot(exists("pitt_raw_host"), exists("sheba_raw_host"))
cat("\nHost rows from §1.4.3:\n")
cat("  Pitt  rows :", nrow(pitt_raw_host),  " | proteins :",
    length(unique(pitt_raw_host$ProteinName)),  "\n")
cat("  Sheba rows :", nrow(sheba_raw_host), " | proteins :",
    length(unique(sheba_raw_host$ProteinName)), "\n")
```

## §18.1 — Summarize host proteins (MSstatsTMT) + matrix + filter

```{r host_summarize, cache=TRUE}
# Same summarization config as §3 (global_norm + reference_norm, MBimpute=FALSE).
# Host has fewer features per protein on average than microbial (Ig hits aside),
# so MSstatsTMT may emit "single feature" warnings — those are informational.

pitt_host_sum <- proteinSummarization(
  data                 = pitt_raw_host,
  method               = "msstats",
  global_norm          = TRUE,
  reference_norm       = TRUE,
  remove_norm_channel  = TRUE,
  remove_empty_channel = TRUE,
  MBimpute             = FALSE,
  use_log_file         = FALSE
)

sheba_host_sum <- proteinSummarization(
  data                 = sheba_raw_host,
  method               = "msstats",
  global_norm          = TRUE,
  reference_norm       = TRUE,
  remove_norm_channel  = TRUE,
  remove_empty_channel = TRUE,
  MBimpute             = FALSE,
  use_log_file         = FALSE
)

cat("Host summarization shapes:\n")
shape_report(pitt_host_sum,  "Pitt  host")
shape_report(sheba_host_sum, "Sheba host")
```

```{r host_matrices}
pitt_host_mat  <- long_to_matrix(pitt_host_sum$ProteinLevelData)
sheba_host_mat <- long_to_matrix(sheba_host_sum$ProteinLevelData)

cat("Host matrices (pre-filter):\n")
cat("  Pitt  : ", dim(pitt_host_mat),  " | missing=",
    round(100*mean(is.na(pitt_host_mat)),  1), "%\n", sep="")
cat("  Sheba : ", dim(sheba_host_mat), " | missing=",
    round(100*mean(is.na(sheba_host_mat)), 1), "%\n", sep="")

# ≥50% detection filter — same threshold as §4 microbial. Host proteins are
# dominated by a few abundant species (Ig, mucins, pancreatic enzymes) and
# many low-prevalence ones, so the filter will be strict.
pitt_host_mat_f  <- filter_by_detection(pitt_host_mat,  0.5)
sheba_host_mat_f <- filter_by_detection(sheba_host_mat, 0.5)

cat("\nHost matrices (post ≥50% detection filter):\n")
cat("  Pitt  : ", nrow(pitt_host_mat_f),  " /", nrow(pitt_host_mat),
    " (", round(100*nrow(pitt_host_mat_f)/nrow(pitt_host_mat), 1), "%)\n",
    sep="")
cat("  Sheba : ", nrow(sheba_host_mat_f), " /", nrow(sheba_host_mat),
    " (", round(100*nrow(sheba_host_mat_f)/nrow(sheba_host_mat), 1), "%)\n",
    sep="")

# Build ID lookup for both cohorts — used in §18.4 cross-cohort and §18.5/6
host_id_pitt  <- parse_host_id(rownames(pitt_host_mat_f))
host_id_sheba <- parse_host_id(rownames(sheba_host_mat_f))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Augment host_id_* with HGNC symbol (resolves the FragPipe-mnemonic-vs-HGNC
# bug discovered in §18.6 first run: FragPipe writes UniProt-mnemonic stems
# like S10A6, K1C19, CATD instead of HGNC symbols S100A6, KRT19, CTSD. The
# panel definitions, msigdbr Hallmarks, and GO:BP all use HGNC, so we have
# to translate.
#
# Strategy: AnnotationDbi::select on org.Hs.eg.db, key=UniProt accession.
# This is the canonical HGNC<->UniProt crosswalk in Bioconductor. Falls back
# to the FragPipe Gene if no HGNC entry (rare; mostly TrEMBL accessions).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_hgnc <- function(host_id_df) {
  uniprots <- unique(host_id_df$UniProt)
  uniprots <- uniprots[!is.na(uniprots) & uniprots != ""]
  hgnc_map <- tryCatch(
    suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
      AnnotationDbi::select(
        org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.eg.db,
        keys      = uniprots,
        columns   = c("UNIPROT","SYMBOL"),
        keytype   = "UNIPROT"))),
    error = function(e) {
      cat("  HGNC lookup error: ", conditionMessage(e),
          " — falling back to FragPipe Gene\n", sep="")
      NULL
    })
  if (is.null(hgnc_map) || nrow(hgnc_map) == 0) {
    return(host_id_df %>% dplyr::mutate(HGNC = Gene))
  }
  # Multiple HGNC symbols per UniProt accession can occur (gene fusion entries,
  # historical aliases). Take the first non-NA per UniProt.
  hgnc_first <- hgnc_map %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(SYMBOL)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(UNIPROT) %>%
    dplyr::slice(1) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::transmute(UniProt = UNIPROT, HGNC = SYMBOL)
  host_id_df %>%
    dplyr::left_join(hgnc_first, by = "UniProt") %>%
    # Fall back to FragPipe Gene if no HGNC mapping
    dplyr::mutate(HGNC = ifelse(is.na(HGNC), Gene, HGNC))
}

host_id_pitt  <- add_hgnc(host_id_pitt)
host_id_sheba <- add_hgnc(host_id_sheba)

cat("HGNC mapping coverage:\n")
cat("  Pitt  : ", sum(host_id_pitt$HGNC  != host_id_pitt$Gene),  " / ",
    nrow(host_id_pitt),  " proteins remapped (",
    round(100*mean(host_id_pitt$HGNC  != host_id_pitt$Gene), 1), "%)\n", sep="")
cat("  Sheba : ", sum(host_id_sheba$HGNC != host_id_sheba$Gene), " / ",
    nrow(host_id_sheba), " proteins remapped (",
    round(100*mean(host_id_sheba$HGNC != host_id_sheba$Gene), 1), "%)\n", sep="")

# Sanity check: did the canonical examples resolve?
sanity_examples <- c("S10A6","S10A8","S10A9","K1C19","CATD","CALL5","ALBU")
sanity_check <- dplyr::bind_rows(host_id_pitt, host_id_sheba) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Gene %in% sanity_examples) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Gene, HGNC)
cat("\nFragPipe → HGNC sanity check (showing detected examples):\n")
print(as.data.frame(sanity_check))

shared_uniprot <- intersect(host_id_pitt$UniProt, host_id_sheba$UniProt)
cat("\nCross-cohort UniProt overlap (post-filter): ",
    length(shared_uniprot), " proteins\n", sep="")
```

## §18.2 — PCA + PERMANOVA per cohort

```{r host_pca, fig.height=4.5}
# Reuse §5's pca_complete_proteins. Note: complete-case set will be small for
# host (high cross-mixture sparsity) — warn-tolerant.
pitt_host_pca  <- pca_complete_proteins(pitt_host_mat_f,  pitt_annot_use)
sheba_host_pca <- pca_complete_proteins(sheba_host_mat_f, sheba_annot_use)

cat("Pitt  host complete-case proteins :", pitt_host_pca$n_complete, "\n")
cat("Sheba host complete-case proteins :", sheba_host_pca$n_complete, "\n")

(plot_pca(pitt_host_pca,  "Pittsburgh — host") |
 plot_pca(sheba_host_pca, "Sheba — host"))
```

```{r host_permanova}
# Two PERMANOVA passes per cohort:
#   (a) unconditional ~ Condition_bin                   -- comparable to §5 microbial
#   (b) Mixture-conditional ~ Condition_bin + Mixture   -- the one we trust
#
# Why both: the §18 first run had Pitt unconditional p=0.008 (R²=2.6%), but
# the per-mixture R/NR balance was pathological — TMT5 was 0NR/10R, TMT2 was
# 9NR/1R, TMT3 was 8NR/2R. Under that imbalance, R-vs-NR is confounded with
# Mixture, so the unconditional p reflects mixture structure, not biology.
# The §5 microbial PERMANOVA was OK at unconditional because §3.1 confirmed
# per-mixture median flatness (±0.3 log2); host complete-case is dominated by
# 2-3 mixtures so that flatness no longer holds.
#
# We keep the unconditional report only for direct comparability against §5;
# the conditional version is the inferential one.

run_permanova_conditional <- function(mat, annot, perm = 999) {
  complete <- mat[complete.cases(mat), , drop = FALSE]
  meta <- annot %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Sample = paste(Mixture, Channel, sep = "_")) %>%
    dplyr::filter(Sample %in% colnames(complete),
                  Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR"))
  meta <- meta[match(colnames(complete)[colnames(complete) %in% meta$Sample],
                     meta$Sample), ]
  meta$Mixture <- factor(meta$Mixture)
  mat_use <- complete[, meta$Sample, drop = FALSE]
  d <- dist(t(mat_use), method = "euclidean")
  # by="margin" gives the marginal effect of Condition_bin AFTER accounting for
  # Mixture, which is what we want.
  vegan::adonis2(d ~ Condition_bin + Mixture,
                 data = meta, by = "margin", permutations = perm)
}

safe_run_permanova <- function(mat, annot, label) {
  complete <- mat[complete.cases(mat), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(complete) < 5) {
    cat(label, "— too few complete-case host proteins (n=", nrow(complete),
        "); skipping PERMANOVA.\n", sep="")
    return(list(unconditional = NULL, conditional = NULL))
  }
  uncond <- tryCatch(
    run_permanova(mat, annot, "Condition_bin"),
    error = function(e) {
      cat(label, "— unconditional PERMANOVA error: ",
          conditionMessage(e), "\n", sep=""); NULL
    })
  cond <- tryCatch(
    run_permanova_conditional(mat, annot),
    error = function(e) {
      cat(label, "— conditional PERMANOVA error: ",
          conditionMessage(e), "\n", sep=""); NULL
    })

  if (!is.null(uncond)) {
    cat("==== ", label, " host PERMANOVA — UNCONDITIONAL ~ Condition_bin\n",
        "    (compare to §5 microbial; not the inferential test for host)\n",
        sep="")
    print(uncond)
  }
  if (!is.null(cond)) {
    cat("\n==== ", label, " host PERMANOVA — CONDITIONAL ~ Condition_bin + Mixture\n",
        "    (inferential — Mixture absorbs the per-plex R/NR imbalance)\n",
        sep="")
    print(cond)

    # Pull the marginal Condition_bin row for diagnostic table
    cond_df <- as.data.frame(cond)
    if ("Condition_bin" %in% rownames(cond_df) && !is.null(uncond)) {
      uncond_df <- as.data.frame(uncond)
      cat("\n  ", label, " Condition_bin effect (unconditional vs conditional):\n",
          "    R²: ", round(uncond_df["Condition_bin","R2"]*100, 2), "% → ",
          round(cond_df["Condition_bin","R2"]*100, 2), "%\n",
          "    p : ", signif(uncond_df["Condition_bin","Pr(>F)"], 3), " → ",
          signif(cond_df["Condition_bin","Pr(>F)"], 3), "\n", sep="")
    }
  }
  list(unconditional = uncond, conditional = cond)
}

permanova_host_pitt  <- safe_run_permanova(pitt_host_mat_f,  pitt_annot_use,
                                            "Pitt ")
permanova_host_sheba <- safe_run_permanova(sheba_host_mat_f, sheba_annot_use,
                                            "Sheba")
```

## §18.3 — Per-cohort DA: limma + permutation

```{r host_limma}
# Reuse §7.2 limma_da unchanged — it's matrix-shape agnostic.
pitt_host_limma  <- limma_da(pitt_host_mat_f,  pitt_annot_use,  "Pitt  host")
sheba_host_limma <- limma_da(sheba_host_mat_f, sheba_annot_use, "Sheba host")
```

```{r host_perm, cache=TRUE}
# Use §7.3's canonical Mixture-stratified permutation. host_complete-case is
# typically dominated by 2-3 mixtures, so many proteins will fail the
# "≥2 mixtures observed" gate inside permutation_da and return NA p-values —
# that's expected and graceful.
pitt_host_perm  <- permutation_da(pitt_host_limma,  "Pitt  host", n_perm = 999)
sheba_host_perm <- permutation_da(sheba_host_limma, "Sheba host", n_perm = 999)
```

```{r host_consensus}
# Per-cohort 2-method consensus: nominal hits in ≥1 method with concordant
# direction between limma logFC and permutation diff_RvsNR.
build_host_consensus <- function(limma_obj, perm_res, label) {
  L <- limma_obj$res
  out <- L %>%
    dplyr::full_join(perm_res, by = "Protein") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      sign_concordant = sign(logFC) == sign(diff_RvsNR) | is.na(diff_RvsNR),
      n_methods_p10   = (p_limma < 0.10 & !is.na(p_limma)) +
                        (p_perm  < 0.10 & !is.na(p_perm)),
      n_methods_q10   = (q_limma < 0.10 & !is.na(q_limma)) +
                        (q_perm  < 0.10 & !is.na(q_perm))
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(p_limma)
  cat(label, "— host consensus: ",
      sum(out$n_methods_p10 >= 2 & out$sign_concordant, na.rm=TRUE),
      " proteins p<0.10 in both methods (concordant), ",
      sum(out$n_methods_q10 >= 1, na.rm=TRUE),
      " with q<0.10 in ≥1 method\n", sep="")
  out
}
pitt_host_consensus  <- build_host_consensus(pitt_host_limma,  pitt_host_perm,
                                              "Pitt ")
sheba_host_consensus <- build_host_consensus(sheba_host_limma, sheba_host_perm,
                                              "Sheba")

# Annotate with gene symbols + write CSVs
pitt_host_consensus <- pitt_host_consensus %>%
  dplyr::left_join(host_id_pitt,  by = c("Protein" = "ProteinName"))
sheba_host_consensus <- sheba_host_consensus %>%
  dplyr::left_join(host_id_sheba, by = c("Protein" = "ProteinName"))

readr::write_csv(pitt_host_consensus,
                 file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "pitt_host_per_cohort_DA.csv"))
readr::write_csv(sheba_host_consensus,
                 file.path(OUT_DIR, "tables", "sheba_host_per_cohort_DA.csv"))

# Show top 15 per cohort
cat("\n==== Pitt host top 15 (by p_limma) ====\n")
print(as.data.frame(pitt_host_consensus %>%
        dplyr::slice_head(n = 15) %>%
        dplyr::select(HGNC, Gene, UniProt, logFC, p_limma, q_limma,
                      diff_RvsNR, p_perm, q_perm)))
cat("\n==== Sheba host top 15 (by p_limma) ====\n")
print(as.data.frame(sheba_host_consensus %>%
        dplyr::slice_head(n = 15) %>%
        dplyr::select(HGNC, Gene, UniProt, logFC, p_limma, q_limma,
                      diff_RvsNR, p_perm, q_perm)))
```

## §18.4 — Cross-cohort meta-analysis (Stouffer's, protein-level)

```{r host_stouffer}
# Stouffer's z-method per UniProt accession, weighted by per-cohort sample size.
# Direction-aware: signed z from limma's per-cohort logFC.
#
# Substrate: proteins detected in BOTH cohorts after §18.1's ≥50% filter.
# Stouffer with sample-size weights:
#   z_i  = signed_p_to_z(p_i, sign(logFC_i))
#   z_c  = sum(w_i * z_i) / sqrt(sum(w_i^2)),  w_i = sqrt(n_i)
#   p_c  = 2 * (1 - pnorm(|z_c|))

signed_p_to_z <- function(p, sgn) {
  # one-sided p in the direction of sgn; convert to z
  p_one <- ifelse(sgn >= 0, p / 2, 1 - p / 2)
  qnorm(1 - p_one)   # positive z = R-up
}

stouffer_combine <- function(p1, lfc1, n1, p2, lfc2, n2) {
  z1 <- signed_p_to_z(p1, sign(lfc1))
  z2 <- signed_p_to_z(p2, sign(lfc2))
  w1 <- sqrt(n1); w2 <- sqrt(n2)
  z_c <- (w1 * z1 + w2 * z2) / sqrt(w1^2 + w2^2)
  p_c <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(z_c))
  tibble::tibble(z_combined = z_c, p_combined = p_c)
}

# Per-cohort sample sizes (R + NR, for weights)
n_pitt  <- sum(pitt_annot_use$Condition_bin  %in% c("R","NR") &
               !duplicated(pitt_annot_use$BioReplicate))
n_sheba <- sum(sheba_annot_use$Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR") &
               !duplicated(sheba_annot_use$BioReplicate))

# Build cross-cohort table: one row per shared UniProt accession.
# Proteins shared can have different ProteinName strings if FragPipe wrote
# slightly different headers (rare; usually IDs are identical).
host_xc <- tibble::tibble(UniProt = shared_uniprot) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    pitt_host_consensus %>%
      dplyr::transmute(UniProt, Gene_pitt = Gene,
                       logFC_pitt = logFC, p_pitt = p_limma, q_pitt = q_limma),
    by = "UniProt") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    sheba_host_consensus %>%
      dplyr::transmute(UniProt, Gene_sheba = Gene,
                       logFC_sheba = logFC, p_sheba = p_limma, q_sheba = q_limma),
    by = "UniProt") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Gene = dplyr::coalesce(Gene_pitt, Gene_sheba),
    direction_concordant = sign(logFC_pitt) == sign(logFC_sheba)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(p_pitt), !is.na(p_sheba))

# Combine
host_xc_combined <- stouffer_combine(
  p1 = host_xc$p_pitt,  lfc1 = host_xc$logFC_pitt, n1 = n_pitt,
  p2 = host_xc$p_sheba, lfc2 = host_xc$logFC_sheba, n2 = n_sheba)
host_xc <- dplyr::bind_cols(host_xc, host_xc_combined) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(q_combined = p.adjust(p_combined, method = "BH")) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(p_combined)

cat("Cross-cohort host meta (Stouffer's, n=", nrow(host_xc), " proteins):\n",
    "  q<0.10 combined        : ", sum(host_xc$q_combined < 0.10, na.rm=TRUE),
    "\n  p<0.10 + concordant    : ",
    sum(host_xc$p_combined < 0.10 & host_xc$direction_concordant, na.rm=TRUE),
    "\n  q<0.10 + concordant    : ",
```
